patches.en:
**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—that. They have passed beyond the presences of the names and attributes, and the self-disclosures peculiar to them, into the open field of essential self-disclosure. They are as the Prophet—God bless him and grant him peace—reported concerning them: ‘A class of the people of Paradise from whom the Lord neither hides nor veils Himself.’ This is because they are not confined within Paradise or any other world or presence. As I have indicated elsewhere, neither Paradise nor anything other than Paradise can encompass a perfect human being. Although they appear in whichever loci of manifestation they will, they transcend confinement, restrictions, places, and times, as does their Master. Rather, they are with Him wherever He is, and where there is neither ‘where’ nor ‘whereabouts’: no body, distance, veil, movement to a visitation, or ending under the ruling of a particular time, name, or attribute. Understand, strive, and aspire to join them and share in some of their exalted ranks, for God is the patron of beneficence.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This corresponds to his earlier statement: “The first of the ranks of the loci in which the divine spirits appear—apart from the perfected—is the imaginal world.” He thus speaks of their concealment in appearing through what we have mentioned: the imaginal world, imagined forms and their food and drink, robes of honour and gifts, the dune of vision, and other things. The generality are different: their state is confined to the presences of the names and attributes, and to the self-disclosures peculiar to them beneath those presences, in the imaginal world and elsewhere. These people have passed beyond the presences of the names and attributes to the open field of essential self-disclosure. They therefore possess the highest ranks of essential affinity, in which the names have no part. They are, as the Prophet—peace be upon him—reported, a class of the people of Paradise from whom the Lord does not hide at any time, or veil Himself in any respect when He discloses Himself to them.

The reason for this absence of hiding and veiling is that they are not restricted to a locus of manifestation, whether Paradise or another world or presence. Everything restricted is narrow, whereas the perfect human being is expansive with the expansiveness of his Lord. He has a locus of manifestation in every place without being confined to it. Thus, although they appear in whatever loci they will, they are not confined to them. Likewise they are not confined to places or times, for otherwise they would be limited by them. They are concealed in appearing in every place and time without restriction. Rather, they are with Him in every place and time, and where there is no place or direction. They have become universal loci for their Lord in all His self-disclosures. Consequently, they have neither distance from Him nor a veil from Him in any respect. Neither do they make a transition for a visitation, since that would particularize a place, and they transcend this—

وسبب عدم التستر والاحتجاب أنهم لا يتقيدون بمظهر سواء الجنة وغيرها من العوالم والحضرات ؛ وذلك لأن كل مقيد ضيق والإنسان الكامل واسع بسعة ربه ، فله بكل مكان مظهر من غير تقيد به ، فهم وإن ظهروا فيما شاءوا من المظاهر لا يتقيدون به ، وكذا لا يتقيدون بالأمكنة والأزمنة ، وإلا تقيدوا بها ، وأنهم لتسترهم في الظهور في كل مكان وزمان ، مع عدم التقيد ، بل هم معه في كل مكان وزمان ، وحيث لامكان ولا جهة ، بل صاروا مظاهر كلية لربهم بجميع تجلياته ، لا جرم لا بعد لهم ولا حجاب عنه بوجه من الوجوه ، فكذا لا انتقال عليهم لزيارة لما فيه من التخصيص بالمكان ، وهم منزهون عنه ،

patches.title: The perfected and unrestricted essential self-disclosure

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —nor does their vision end under the ruling of a particular time, for they have passed beyond times; nor under the ruling of the names and attributes that require distinction, for they have passed beyond the presences of the names and attributes. Understand. They are with the Real in all things. Strive to join them in some of their exalted ranks by following them—indeed, to share independently with them in this. God is the patron of beneficence, so do not look at your own deficiency and thereby cease this striving.

**Qūnawī:** “As for the affinities established among people in respect of their intermediate ranks, their model—which draws the attention of one who has neither unveiled nor witnessed them to their details—is what the Prophet—God bless him and grant him peace—mentioned in the report of the Night Journey: he saw Adam, peace be upon him, in the lowest heaven, with the dark forms of the felicitous among his descendants to his right and those of the wretched to his left. When he looked to his right he laughed, and when he looked to his left he wept. This points to the ranks of the generality of the wretched and the felicitous.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This indicates the third of the forms of affinity pertaining to rank: those upon which the intermediate condition rests, the barzakh between this world and the greater Resurrection—that is, the states of the grave. He gives as a model of this affinity what the Prophet mentioned in the report of the Night Journey. This model draws attention to the details of those affinities, which are ordered according to their higher and lower stations. Only one who has neither unveiled nor witnessed them needs this indication; otherwise he has no need of the report. The Prophet saw Adam in the lowest heaven so that Adam might oversee the division of his children into higher and lower groups. For this reason, the dispatch of those destined for the Fire is entrusted to him on the Day of Resurrection. His laughter expresses his satisfaction with the dark forms of the felicitous. His weeping expresses his grief for them on seeing their deficiency. His right signifies the essential side, because it is the strong side [a short phrase here is unclear in the print]; the strong is more favoured than the weak. Understand from this report that in the barzakh the abode of the wretched is beneath the lowest heaven, while the felicitous are above that.

He then indicates the details, saying:

**Qūnawī:** “The people of wretchedness are those for whom the gates of heaven were not opened at death. They have different ranks in their wretchedness. The Prophet—salutations upon him and his household—reported that the spirits of some of the wretched are gathered in Barahūt, al-Ḥalīyatayn, al-Khāsiʾayn—”

ولا انتهاء لرؤيتهم بحكم وقت من الأوقات ؛ لأنهم جاوزوا الأزمنة ، ولا بحكم الأسماء والصفات القاضية بالامتياز ؛ لأنهم تجاوزوا حضرات الأسماء والصفات ، فافهم . 
فإنهم مع الحق في الكل ، واجتهد أن تلحق بهم في بعض مراتبهم العالية بتبعيتهم ، بل وأن تشاركهم في ذلك بالاستقلال ، واللّه ولي الإحسان ، فلا تنظر إلى قصورك فتنقطع عن هذا الجهد ) .

وذلك ليتولى القسم بين أولاده علوا وسفلا ، فلذلك يفوض إليه بعث النار يوم القيامة ، وضحكه عبارة عن رضاه عن أسودة السعداء ، وبكاؤه عبارة عن حزنه عليهم لرؤية نقصانه ، ويمينه عبارة عن الجانب الذاتي ؛ لأنه الجانب القوي أنا لها ، والقوي أحلى من الضعيف ، فافهم هذا الحديث ، أن الأشقياء يكون منزلهم تحت السماء الدنيا ، في البرزخ ، وأن السعداء فوق ذلك . 

وهذا عن تفاصيل إليها أشار الشيخ فقال رضي اللّه عنه : [ فأهل الشقاء هم الذين لم تفتح لهم أبواب السماء حال الموت ، وهم في شقائهم على مراتب مختلفة ؛ فإن النبي عليه وعلى آل بيته التحية : أخبر عن أرواح بعض الأشقياء أنها تجمع في برهوت  “ 2  “ والحليتين والخاسئين

patches.title: Intermediate ranks and Adam in the lowest heaven

patches.en:
**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—and al-Khābitayn. The ranks of the wretched begin at the concave inner surface of the lowest heaven, in which Adam is, and their lowest rank is what he—peace be upon him—mentioned. The ranks of the generality of the felicitous in the barzakh are in the lowest heaven, at differing degrees gathered within a single rank. The ranks of the elect among the felicitous are those to which he pointed in the report of the Night Journey after mentioning Adam: Jesus is in the second heaven, Joseph in the third, Idrīs in the fourth, Aaron in the fifth, Moses in the sixth, and Abraham in the seventh—peace upon them all. The same applies to those who fully share with these prophets and inherit from them, at differing ranks within these heavens. These reports from the Messenger—God bless him and grant him peace—concern what he witnessed during one of his night journeys. For it is established that the Prophet experienced thirty-four ascents, whose reports Abū Nuʿaym, the traditionist of Isfahan—God have mercy upon him—transmitted, collected, and authenticated.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, since he saw the dark forms of the wretched to Adam's left, the gates of heaven were not opened to any of the wretched when they died. They have no heavenly locus of manifestation, and their wretchedness has different ranks.

The Prophet reported that the spirits of some of them are gathered in Barahūt and al-Khāsiʾayn. These are well-known transmitted accounts. Their rank in wretchedness is therefore the sphere of earth. Yet the report of the Night Journey states that they are beneath the lowest heaven, which implies that they are in the sphere of ether.

The way to reconcile the two, indicating their different ranks, is that the ranks of the wretched begin at the concave inner surface of the lowest heaven. Their highest rank, for those whose wretchedness is least, is the sphere of ether, because they are close to Adam in disobedience and in hope of forgiveness. Their lowest rank is what the Prophet mentioned: some are gathered in Barahūt and al-Khābitayn.

He then mentions that the ranks of the generality of the felicitous—that is, those who had wretchedness [the printed phrase is awkward]—are, in the world of the barzakh, the lowest heaven. He qualifies this by ‘in the barzakh’ because at the Resurrection they will be in Paradise above those abodes. Within the lowest heaven they also have differing ranks, although they share its single rank. This is because they combined obedience and disobedience and obtained forgiveness, like Adam. patches.title: Degrees of wretchedness and felicity in the barzakh

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —the elect among the felicitous are above that. Even if they committed acts of disobedience, these were replaced with good deeds and so were not taken into account. This is as the Prophet reported concerning these prophets. The same applies to the perfected among their heirs and followers, although their ranks also differ. He explains that, because they are people of perfection, they are not confined there; these are only some of their loci of manifestation. The Messenger's reports concern some of what he witnessed during some of his ascents.

**Qūnawī:** “How could this condition be confined to these seven prophets, to the exclusion of others? It is clear that the messengers and prophets are many, and among them are perfected ones identified by God, such as David, whose vicegerency is explicitly stated, and other great prophets who were messengers. Where, then, are their intermediate ranks determined after death? [The printed transition to the upper and lower worlds is defective.] The lower world is the locus in which the ranks of the wretched are determined, in all their differences. It follows that the levels at which the ranks of the prophets and messengers, the perfected among their heirs, and the elect among the felicitous are determined after death and before the gathering must be in the heavenly presences. What occasioned the Prophet's statement is what has already been indicated: it is a model of what was not individually mentioned. Understand.

“This particular report from the Prophet concerning these seven was occasioned only by a state, an affinity in attributes, acts, or state. It is as with John, peace be upon him, who is sometimes with Jesus and sometimes with Aaron, peace upon them all. This follows only from his sharing with both of them. Reflect, and you will be guided, if God wills.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Nor is the establishment of those ascents for the Prophet precluded. How, then, could this condition—that is, determination in the heavens—be confined to these seven, when the messengers and prophets are numerous and the perfected are not confined to these seven? Consider David: God—mighty and majestic—explicitly stated his vicegerency, saying, “O David, We have appointed you a vicegerent” [Q 38:26]. He said of Adam, “I am appointing a vicegerent on earth” [Q 2:30]. How, then, could David be below him? The same applies to other great prophets and messengers. Aaron was not one of the messengers; if he had a determination in the heavens, how could the messengers lack one? If their ranks were not determined in the heavens, where would their intermediate ranks be determined after death and before the Resurrection, when in—

خواص السعداء فوق ذلك ، وإن كانت لهم معاص لكنها بدلت بالحسنات ، فلم يعبأ بها . 
كما أخبر عليه السلام عن هؤلاء الأنبياء ، وهكذا شأن الكمّل من ورثتهم وأتباعهم مع اختلافهم أيضا في المرتبة ، ذكر أنهم لكونهم من أهل الكمال لا ينحصرون هناك ، بل هي بعض مظاهرهم ، فإن هذه الأخبار من الرسول صلى اللّه عليه وسلم باعتبار بعض مشاهداته الحاصلة في بعض معاريجه . 

قال الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه : [ وكيف ينحصر هذا الحال مع هؤلاء الأنبياء السبعة دون غيرهم ، ومن البيّن أن الرسل والأنبياء كثيرون ، وفيهم الكمّل بتعريف اللّه ، كداوود عليه السلام المنصوص على خلافته ، وغيره من أكابر الأنبياء المرسلين ، فأين تتعين مراتبهم البرزخية بعد الموت ، ومن ثم إلى العالم الأعلى الأسفل ، وعالم السفلى محل تعينات مراتب الأشقياء على اختلافهم ، فتعين أن تكون طبقات تعينات مراتب الأنبياء والمرسلين ، والكمّل من ورثتهم وأهل الخصوص من السعداء بعد الموت ، وقبل الحشر في الحضرات السماوية ، وأن موجب ما ذكره عليه وعلى آله السلام - هو ما سبقت الإشارة إليه ، فهو كالأنموذج لما لم يتعين ذكره ، فافهم . 
فهذه الرواية الخاصة من النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم لهؤلاء السبعة إنما موجبها حالة إذ مناسبة صفاتية أو فعلية أو حالية لا غير ، كالأمر في شأن يحيى عليه السلام من أن يكون تارة مع عيسى عليه السلام ، وتارة مع هارون عليه السلام ، وليس ذلك إلا مقتضى مشاركته لهما - على جميعهم السلام - فتدبّر ترشد إن شاء اللّه تعالى ] .

وليس منع ثبوت تلك المعاريج له صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ، فكيف ينحصر هذا الحال ، أي : التعين في السماويات في هؤلاء السبعة مع كثرة الرسل والأنبياء ، والحال أن الكمل غير منحصرة في هؤلاء السبعة كداوود عليه السلام ، إن نصر عزّ وجلّ على خلافته بقوله : يا داوُدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْناكَ خَلِيفَةً [ ص : 26 ] .

وقد قال عزّ وجلّ في حق آدم : إِنِّي جاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً [ البقرة : 30 ] ، فكيف يكون دونه ، وكذا غيره من أكابر الأنبياء والمرسلين ، مع أن هارون ليس من المرسلين ، فإذا كان له تعين في السماويات ، فكيف لا يكون للمرسلين ذلك ، فإن لم يكن تعين مراتبهم في السماوات ، فأين تتعين مراتبهم البرزخية بعد الموت قبل القيامة ، وليس في

patches.title: Why heavenly ranks are not confined to seven prophets

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —reality there are only the upper, heavenly world and the lower, elemental world in which they could be determined? The lower world is the locus of the determination of the ranks of the wretched, according to their differing levels. How could the felicitous—indeed, the prophets and the perfected among their descendants—share those ranks with them? Nor can their ranks be determined in those [paradisal] abodes, because that belongs specifically to what follows the gathering.

It follows that the ranks of the prophets and messengers, the perfected saints among their heirs, and the elect among the felicitous—even those who have not reached the ranks of the saints—are, after death and before the gathering, in the heavenly presences. How, then, could they be confined to the prophets named? Rather, the reason why the Prophet mentioned these seven is what has already been indicated: this was one of his visions. What he stated in that report is a model of what was not individually specified. They were, however, mentioned collectively, since he placed the dark forms of the felicitous to Adam's right, indicating that they are in the heavens.

He then states the cause of this particular witnessing. In that state, an affinity of those prophets with those heavens predominated—an affinity in attributes, acts, or state, not an essential one. Otherwise they would never change from those heavens. But this is not so, as with John, who is sometimes with Jesus and sometimes with Aaron. This difference follows from his sharing [with them; the following printed wording is difficult]. Essential affinity does not change. Moreover, taking the differing reports to be sound indicates a plurality of ascents. Hence the shaykh says, “Reflect, and you will be guided”: that is, as their sharing in those attributes and states is, so are their determinations in the heavens.

**Text Twenty-One**

**Qūnawī:** “A very noble text.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** In the previous text he mentioned the Real and creation, their ranks, and their essential affinities and affinities of rank. He now mentions the divine unity that gathers all of them, without the Real veiling creation or creation veiling the Real. Its nobility comes from this station's exalted rank above the other stations. It is ‘very’ noble because it is the return and end of all of them.

**Qūnawī:** “Know that the Real is pure existence, in which there is no difference. He is one with a true unity that is not conceived in opposition to multiplicity, and whose realization in itself or conception in knowledge does not depend—”

الواقع لتعينها إلا العالم الأعلى السماوي ، والعالم الأسفل العنصري ، والعالم السفلي محل تعينات مراتب الأشقياء على اختلاف طبقاتهم ، فكيف يشارك السعداء بل الأنبياء والكمّل من ذريتهم في تلك المراتب ، ولا يمكن أن يكون تعينات مراتبهم في تلك المنازل ؛ لأن ذلك يختص بما بعد الحشر . 

فتعين أن يكون مراتب الأنبياء والمرسلين والكمّل من ورثتهم من الأولياء ، وأهل الخصوص من السعداء ، وإن لم يبلغوا مراتب الأولياء بعد الموت ، وقبل الحشر في الحضرات السماوية ، فأين يصح الحصر في الأنبياء المذكورين ، بل موجب ما ذكره النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم لهؤلاء الأنبياء السبعة هو ما سبق الإشارة إليه من أنه في بعض مشاهداتهم مما ذكره عليه السلام في ذلك الحديث كالأنموذج لما لم يتعين ، أي : لم يذكره على التعين ، لكنهم مذكورون على الجملة إذ جعل عليه أسودة السعداء عن يمينه ، فدل على أنهم في السماوات . 
ثم ذكر ما هو سبب هذه المشاهدة الخاصة ، بل موجبها في تلك الحالة غلبت مناسبة لأولئك الأنبياء مع تلك السماوات ، صفاتية أو فعلية أو حالية لا ذاتية ، وألا يتغيروا عن تلك السماوات أصلا ، لكنه ليس كذلك كالأمر في شأن يحيى عليه السلام من أن يكون مع عيسى ، وتارة مع هارون ، وليس ذلك الاختلاف فيه إلا من مقتضى مشاركته الذاتية لا تتغير ، على أنه يدل على تعدد المعاريج حمل الروايات المختلفة على الصحة ؛ 
فلذلك قال الشيخ : ( فتدبر ترشد ) أي : أن حال مشاركتهم في تلك الصفات والأحوال كذلك يكون تعيناتهم في السماوات .

النص الحادي والعشرون
قال رضوان اللّه عليه : [ نص شريف جدّا ] لما ذكر في النص السابق الحق والخلق ، ومراتبهم ومناسبتهم الذاتية والمرتبية ، ذكر ما يجمع الكل من التوحيد من غير أن يحجب الحق الخلق ، ولا الخلق الحق ، وشرفه بعلو مرتبة هذا المقام على سائر المقامات ، وكونه جدّا لكونه مرجع الكل وغايته . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ اعلم أن الحق هو الوجود المحض لا اختلاف فيه ، وإنه واحد وحدة حقيقية لا يتعقل في مقابلة كثرة ، ولا يتوقف تحققها في نفسها ، ولا تصورها في العلم

patches.title: Heavenly affinities and the opening of Text Twenty-One

patches.en:
**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—in sound, realized knowledge upon conceiving an opposite to it. Rather, it is established through itself and establishes [others]; it is not established [by another]. Our saying ‘unity’ is for declaring transcendence and conveying understanding, not for indicating the concept of unity as it is conceived in veiled minds.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, the Real in the first determination and the essential forms of knowledge is pure existence. He did not say ‘abstract existence,’ since there He is not restricted to manifestation or hiddenness. There is no difference within Him through the realization of two things, such as quiddity and existence, or the absolute and its restrictions.

Pure existence is one because it is necessary through itself and admits no plurality. Its unity is real, not a relative unity opposed to multiplicity. How could it be conceived in opposition to multiplicity, which is the opposite of unity, when it has no opposite at all? Otherwise its realization in the mind would depend on its opposite there. Nor does its realization in itself depend on its opposite, for then the Necessary would depend on another; nor does its conception in sound knowledge depend on conceiving an opposite. He explains ‘sound’ by ‘realized’: knowledge obtained through unveiling. This differs from the knowledge of veiled theologians, who required demonstrations of divine unity to establish it. They conceived unity in opposition to multiplicity, imagined it to be additional to the Essence, and established it by demonstrations on the model of something accruing to the Essence. But it is not so. Rather, unity is established through itself, externally and mentally; it establishes what is other than itself and is not established by another, such as their demonstrations.

He then anticipates a question: the Essence as such can be conceived as one or many, so how can unity be identical with it? He answers that our saying ‘unity’ declares transcendence beyond the multiplicity imagined by the veiled, and conveys that this Essence is pure existence itself. Unity is coextensive with existence: every existent possesses unity, even the many—not insofar as it is many, but insofar as there is multiplicity within it, for unity accrues to multiplicity.

It may be said: existence, but not unity, accrues to the many insofar as it is many. We answer: when unity accrues to the multiplicity within it, it thereby accrues mediately to the many. The difference of aspects is an intellectual matter.

It may be said: if unity were existence itself, division would be annihilation; but that is false, for the cleaving—

الصحيح المحقق على تصور ضد لها ، بل هي لنفسها ثابتة مثبتة لا مثبتة . 
وقولنا : وحدة للتنزيه والتفهيم لا للدلالة على مفهوم الوحدة على نحو ما هو متصور في الأذهان المحجوبة ] . 
أي : الحق في التعين الأول  “ 1  “ ، والصور العلمية الذاتية هو الوجود المحض ، لم يقل هو المجرد ، إذ هو فيه وثمة لا يتقيد بالظهور والبطون لا اختلاف فيه بتحقق شيئين : 
الماهية والوجود ، أو المطلق والقيود . 
والوجود المحض واحد ؛ لأنه الواجب لذاته ولا تعدد فيه ، وحدة حقيقية لا إضافية مقابل الكثرة ، وكيف يتعقل في مقابلة الكثرة وهي ضد الوحدة ، وليس لها ضد أصلا وإلا توقف تحققها ذهنا على توقف ضدها فيه ، ولا يتوقف تحققها في نفسها على ضدها ، وإلا لزم توقف الواجب على الغير ، ولا تصورها في العلم الصحيح ، وفسّر الصحيح بالمحقق للحاصل بالكشف على تصور ضد لها ، بخلاف علم المحجوبين من المتكلمين حتى افتقروا في إثباته إلى أدلة التوحيد ؛ وذلك لأنهم تصوروا الوحدة في مقابل الكثرة ، فتصوروها زائدة على الذات ، فأثبتوها بالأدلة على النهج عروضها للذات ، وليس كذلك ، بل هي بنفسها ثابتة خارجا وذهنا ، مثبتة لما سواها لا مثبتة بالغير كأدلتهم . 

ثم استشعر سؤالا بأن الذات من حيث هي يمكن تعقل واحدة وكثيرة ، فكيف الوحدة عينها . 
فأجاب بأن قولنا : وحدة للتنزيه عن الكثرة المتوهمة للمحجوبين ، وتفهم أن تلك الذات نفس الوجود المحض ، إذ الوحدة تساوق الوجود ، فكل موجود له وحدة حتى الكثير لا من حيث هو كثير ، بل من حيث فيه كثرة ، والوحدة تعرض الكثرة . 
قيل : الكثير من حيث هو كثير يعرض له الوجود دون الوحدة . 

قلنا : لما عرضت الكثرة التي فيه ، فقد عرضت للكثير بالواسطة ، وتغاير الجهات أمر عقلي . 
قيل : لو كانت نفس الوجود ، لكان التفريق إعداما وهو باطل ، إذ ليس شق

patches.title: True unity, conceptual opposition, and the theologians

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —of the green sea by a mosquito with its needle plainly does not annihilate it and bring two other seas into being.

We answer: division could be annihilation only if it [negated] unity; the sea's unity remains. Suppose we grant that it becomes many: it has then ceased to be in respect of unity. The origination of two seas—that is, a quality assigned to two seas before their origination—cannot be sheer nonexistence, even if it is other than existence. Thus he did not mean to indicate the concept of unity opposed to multiplicity, in which its subject is supposed to be an individual admitting no division. Unity and multiplicity are united in Him without the Essence of the Necessary—exalted is He—becoming multiple.

**Qūnawī:** “Once you know this, we say: He—glory be to Him—in respect of the unity to which attention has been drawn, and His detachment from the loci of manifestation and from the descriptions attributed to Him through those loci and His manifestation in them, is not apprehended, encompassed, known, characterized, or described.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, once you know that He is pure existence without difference and that His unity is not opposed to multiplicity, we say that the Real—glory and exaltation be to Him—in respect of the unity indicated is not fully apprehended. He qualifies the statement this way because knowledge of Him is possible from the standpoint of the unity He has in the attributes. Complete apprehension would require distinguishing Him from what is other than Him; how could what has no opposite be distinguished from what is other than it? Nor is He encompassed by an essential definition: there are no intrinsic constituents within Him to be defined through differences of genus and differentia in His Essence. Nor is there a descriptive definition, since concomitants are not taken into account in that presence. He is not characterized by a characterization distinguishing Him intrinsically, or described by a description distinguishing Him accidentally, since these are not taken into account there. The same applies in respect of His detachment from the loci of manifestation, which are His attributes under one consideration, though not in respect of His Essence: He is then not restricted by anything that distinguishes Him. Everything we have mentioned concerns distinction. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “Everything apprehended in entities and witnessed among created things, however a human being apprehends it and in whatever presence the witnessing occurs—apart from the apprehension of abstract meanings and realities in their unseen presence by unveiling, which is why I said ‘in entities’—that is, whatever is apprehended in a locus of manifestation, consists only of colours, lights, and surfaces differing in quality and quantity, which appear, or whose likenesses appear, in the imaginal world connected with the human constitution or separate from it in one respect, according to what exists externally or whose constituent elements exist externally. The multiplicity of all these is sensed, while their oneness is intellectually grasped or intuited. All this consists of the rulings of existence—or say, the forms of the relations of His knowledge, or attributes inseparable from it—in respect of—”

البعوض بإبرة البحر الأخضر إعداما له ، وإحداثا لبحرين آخرين ضرورة . 
قلنا : إنما يمكن التفريق إعداما لو كان مبدأ للوحدة ، فإن وحدة البحر أيضا باقية ، سلمنا أنه يكثر ، فقد عدم من حيث الوحدة ، وإحداث البحرين ، أي : صفة جعلت لبحرين قبل الأحداث لا يكون محض عدم ، وإن كانت غير الوجود ، فلم يذكر الدلالة على مفهوم الوحدة المقابلة للكثرة ، وهي أن يكون مفروضها شخصا لا يقبل القسمة بالوحدة والكثرة ، فيه يتحدان من غير أن تتعدد ذات الواجب تعالى . 

قال الشيخ الكبير رضي اللّه عنه : [ وإذا عرفت هذا ، فنقول أنه سبحانه من حيث اعتبار وحدته المنبه عليها ، وتجرده عن المظاهر وعن الأوصاف المضافة إليه من حيث المظاهر وظهوره فيها ، لا يدرك ولا يحاط به ولا يعرف ولا ينعت ولا يوصف ] . 

أي : إذا عرفت أنه محض الوجود لا اختلاف فيه ، وأن وحدته ليست في مقابلة الكثرة ، فنقول : أن الحق سبحانه وتعالى من حيث اعتبار وحدته المنبه عليها قيد بذلك ؛ لإمكان معرفته من جهة الوحدة التي له في الصفات التي لا يدرك إدراكا تاما ؛ لأنه يقتضي تميزه عما عداه ، وما لا ضد له كيف تميز عما عداه ولا يحاط به بالتعريف الحدّي ، إذ لا ذاتيات فيه لتعريفها على الاختلاف في ذاته من الجنس والفصل ، ولا التعريف الرسمي ، إذ لا عبرة للوازم في تلك الحضرة ، بل ولا ينعت نعتا يميزه بوجه ذاتي ، ولا يوصف بوصف يميزه بوجه عرضي ، إذ لا عبرة لها ، وهكذا من حيث اعتبار تجرده عن المظاهر ، وهي أوصافه باعتبار ، ولا باعتبار ذاته ، إذ لا يتقيد بشيء تميزه حينئذ ، وجميع ما ذكرناه باعتبار التميز ، فافهم . 

قال الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه : [ وكل ما يدرك في الأعيان ، ويشهد من الأكوان بأي وجه كان أدركه الإنسان ، وفي أي حضرة حصل الشهود ، ما عدا الإدراك المتعلق بالمعاني المجردة والحقائق في حضرة غيبها بطريق الكشف ؛ ولذلك قلت في الأعيان ، أي : ما أدرك في مظهر ما كان ، فإنما ذلك المدرك ألوان وأضواء وسطوح مختلفة الكيفية متفاوتة الكمية ، تظهر أو مثلتها في عالم المثال المتصل بنشأة الإنسان أو المنفصل عنه من وجه على نحو ما هو في الخارج ، أو ما مفرداته في الخارج ، وكثرة الجميع محسوسة ، والأحدية فيها معقولة أو محدوسة ، وكل ذلك أحكام الوجود أو قل صور نسب علمه أو صفات لازمة له بحيث

patches.title: The sea analogy and the limits of apprehending pure existence

patches.en:
**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—its association with each existent entity through the secret of its manifestation. It appears in it, through it, for it, and according to it. However you wish to put it, what is thus named is not existence itself.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This answers an implicit question: you said that existence in respect of its unity is neither apprehended nor known, and also that unity belongs to it intrinsically and is among its coextensive concomitants. Yet we sense it in entities and created things, and know it in abstract meanings and realities in their unseen presence by unveiling.

He answers: apprehension either concerns abstract meanings and unseen realities, which are intellectual things without existence—so how can existence be apprehended in them? Unveiling apprehends them in their unseen presence, which is nonexistent—or it concerns entities. Everything apprehended in entities, whether a human being—the most complete of apprehenders—apprehends it through intellect, spirit, heart, outward senses, or inward senses, and likewise whatever is witnessed among created things in any divine or created presence, must be in a locus of manifestation, whether sensible or spiritual.

What is directly apprehended is colours and lights, and incidentally surfaces differing in quality through their differing colours. Difference in quantity does not entail that apprehension of the surfaces [the printed construction here is awkward]. This concerns outward sense.

As for inward sense, what is apprehended is their likenesses. Those likenesses are in the imaginal world connected with the human constitution: the imagination, which is in the front of the brain. Or they are in the imaginal world separate from the human being in one respect, because it is not one of his faculties but is in the sphere of the zodiacal constellations. It is nevertheless connected with him in another respect, since without it he would not apprehend at all. Those likenesses appear in one of the two worlds in accordance with the external things they represent: likenesses of the colours, lights, and surfaces mentioned. Or [their elements] are externally established, as in the case of a sea of mercury.

Sensing and apprehending these is not sensing and apprehending existence. The multiplicity of them all is sensed, especially in surfaces differing in quality and quantity. The oneness concomitant with existence in them is intellectually grasped or intuited—that is, apprehended by intellect or intuition. Thus, when the unity coextensive with existence is not apprehended, existence is not apprehended either.

Do not say: ‘You have said that their unity is intellectually grasped or intuited, so it has been apprehended, and consequently—’

اقترانه بكل عين موجودة بسر ظهوره ، فيظهر فيها وبها ولها بحسبها كيف شئت ، وأطلقت ليس هو الوجود ] . 

جواب سؤال مقدر تقديره : إنكم قلتم أن الوجود من حيث وحدته لا يدرك ولا يعرف ، وقد قلتم أيضا : أن الوحدة ثابتة له بالذات ، ومن لوازمه المساوقة ، ونحن نحس به في الأعيان والأكوان ، ونعرفه في المعاني المجردة والحقائق في حضرة غيبها بطريق الكشف . 

فأجاب بأن : الإدراك إما متعلق بالمعاني المجردة والحقائق الغيبية ، فهي أمور عقلية لا وجود لها ، فكيف يدرك فيها الوجود والكشف إنما يدرك في حضرة غيبها وهي عدمية ، وإما بالأعيان ، فكل ما يدرك في الأعيان سواء أدركه الإنسان الذي هو أكمل المدركين بعقله أو بروحه أو بقلبه أو بحواسه الظاهرة أو الباطنة ، وكذا ما يشهد من الأكوان ، أي : 
في حضرة من الحضرات الحقيّة والخلقية ، حصل الشهود ، لا بدّ وأن يكون في مظهر ، سواء كان من المظاهر الحسية أو الروحانية . 
فالمدرك بالذات من ذلك إنما هو الألوان والأضواء ، وبالعرض السطوح مختلفة الكيفية باختلاف ألوانها ، فتفاوت الكمية لا يستلزم إدراك السطوح ذلك - هذا - في الحس الظاهر . 

وأما الباطن فالمدرك أمثلتها ، تلك الأمثلة في عالم المثال المتصل بنشأة الإنسان ، وهو الخيال الذي هو في مقدم الدماغ ، أو عالم المثال المنفصل عن الإنسان من وجه لكونه ليس من قواه ، بل في فلك البروج ، لكنه متصل به من وجه آخر ، إذ لولاه لم يدرك أصلا بتلك الأمثلة تظهر في أحد العالمين على نحو ما هي أمثلته في الخارج ، فتظهر أمثلة الألوان والأضواء والسطوح المذكورة ، 
أو على ما تقرر ذاته في الخارج لبحر من الزئبق فالإحساس بذلك وإدراكها ليس بإحساس ، وأدرك للوجود ؛ لأن كثرة الجميع محسوسة سيما في السطوح المختلفة الكيفية ، المختلفة المتفاوتة الكمية ؛ والأحدية اللازمة للوجود فيها معقولة أو محدوسة ، أي : يدركه بالعقل أو بالحدس ، فإذا لم يدرك الوحدة المساوقة للوجود ، لم يدرك الوجود أيضا .

patches.title: Outward sense, inward imagination, and what each apprehends

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —‘existence has been apprehended.’ For we answer: complete apprehension is intended, and it has not been apprehended in that way, but only generally. Moreover, this unity apprehended in the things is not the unity of existence, which is not apprehended in them at all. Since what is seen of these things is not existence itself, we say that all this apprehended content is the rulings of existence in respect of its association with each entity to which existence is attributed. This association is not by contact, but through the secret of its appearing in them—that is, in their realities—and its appearing when they see it in another, as you see it in the horizons and in yourselves. It appears through them for themselves or for another, and according to them, not in its totality as it is. Hence its manifestation differs in the human being and in other things.

Or we say: all this apprehended content is the forms of the relations of His knowledge—that is, the realities within it—in respect of its association with each of those realities, and so forth. Or you say: they are attributes inseparable from it in respect of the association mentioned. The difference between this and ‘rulings’ and ‘forms’ is that attributes pertain to the Essence, even through another description; rulings may pertain to attributes alone; while forms must be peculiar to the attributes, not within the attributes but within their loci of manifestation. Say and designate it however you wish.

The result is that what is apprehended is not existence, which is the one Real insofar as He is one. The shaykh then gives the reason:

**Qūnawī:** “Existence is one, and is not apprehended by what is other than it insofar as the other differs from it. As already stated, the one insofar as it is one is not apprehended by the many insofar as they are many, and conversely. Apprehension is not possible for the human being insofar as he is one with a true unity like the unity of existence. Rather, it is possible insofar as he is a reality qualified by existence and life, with knowledge subsisting in him, an affinity established between him and what he intends to apprehend, and the obstacles preventing apprehension removed. He apprehends what he apprehends only through his multiplicity, not through his oneness. His apprehension of that in which there is no multiplicity at all is therefore impossible, for the reason already given. This point has secrets concerning the soul, which I have discussed in greater detail in my book *Uncovering the Veil of Jealousy from the Secret of Perplexity*. Later in this book there will also be further clarification of what we have stated and established, if God—exalted is He—wills.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Existence is not apprehended in them because it is one, and the one is not apprehended by the many insofar as they are many: they differ from it; difference is separation, and separation prevents knowledge, as stated in Text Eleven.

الوجود ؛ لأنّا نقول : المراد الإدراك التام ، ولم يدرك كذلك ، بل في الجملة ؛ على أن هذه الوحدة المدركة فيها ليست هي وحدة الوجود ، فإنها لا تدرك فيها أصلا ، وإذا لم يكن المرئي من هذه الأشياء نفس الوجود ، فنقول كل ذلك المدرك أحكام الوجود من حيث اقترانه لكل عين أضيف إليه الوجود ، وليس ذلك الاقتران بطريق الاتصال ، بل بسر ظهوره فيها ، 
أي : في حقائقها ، وظهوره إذا هي تراه في غيره ، كما ترى في الآفاق والأنفس ؛ ويظهر بها لذاتها أو لغيره وبحسبها لا بكليته ؛ كما هو ، فلذلك يتفاوت ظهور في الإنسان وغيره . 

أو نقول : كل ذلك المدرك صور نسب علمه ، أي : الحقائق التي فيه من حيث اقترانه بكل من تلك الحقائق إلى آخره . 
أو تقول صفات لازمة له من حيث اقترانه المذكور ، والفرق بين هذا وبين الأحكام والصور ، أن الصفات تتعلق بالذات وله بواسطة وصف آخر ، والأحكام يجوز تعلقها بالصفات فقط ، والصور لا بدّ وأن تختص بالصفات لا فيها ، بل في مظاهرها كيف شئت وأطلقت ، فقل وأطلق . 

والحاصل أن ذلك المدرك ليس الوجود الذي هو الحق الواحد من حيث هو واحد ، 

ثم علله الشيخ ، فقال : [ فإن الوجود واحد ، ولا يدرك بسواه من حيث ما يغايره على ما مر من أن الواحد من كونه واحدا لا يدرك بالكثير من حيث هو كثير وبالعكس ، ولم يصح الإدراك للإنسان من كونه واحدا وحدة حقيقية كوحدة الوجود ، بل إنما صح له ذلك من كونه حقيقية متصفة بالوجود والحياة وقيام العلم به ، وثبوت المناسبة بينه وبين ما يروم إدراكه وارتفاع الموانع العائقة عن الإدراك ، 
فما أدرك ما أدركه إلا من حيث كثرته ، لا من حيث أحديته ، فتعذر إدراكه من حيث هو ما لا كثرة فيه أصلا لما مر . ولهذه النكتة أسرار نفسية ذكرتها بتفصيل أكثر من هذا في كتابي المسمي بكشف ستر الغيرة عن سر الحيرة ، وسيرد أيضا في داخل الكتاب ما يزيد بيانا لما ذكرناه وأصلناه إن شاء اللّه تعالى ] . 

أي إنما لم يدرك الوجود فيها ؛ لأنه واحد ولا يدرك الواحد بالكثير من حيث هو كثير ؛ لأنه يغايره ، والمغايرة مباينة ، والمباينة مانعة من العلم على ما مر في النص الحادي عشر .

patches.title: Rulings of existence and the multiplicity involved in knowing

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** For this reason the many are not apprehended by the one insofar as it is one. Moreover, if the one were apprehended by the many, forms would be impressed according to the parts of the many, and it would be apprehended as many. If the many were apprehended by the one, they would be represented in the one, which is impossible because the one has no capacity for the representation of the many within it. Yet the one may be apprehended by the many through a single aspect [the following construction is compressed], and the many by unity insofar as the one encompasses them potentially.

Hence he said, “It is not apprehended by what is other than it insofar as the other differs from it,” and, “insofar as it is one.” He then anticipates the question: why may the human being not apprehend it in respect of his unity? The many insofar as they possess unity may apprehend the one; that is why the earlier prohibition was qualified by ‘in respect of multiplicity.’ He answers that the human being's apprehension of the Real is not through his being one with a true unity like the unity of existence, since he has no such unity. Even if this is granted, he apprehends only through multiplicity: his qualification by existence involves quiddity and existence; in addition to these two, life is required, since the dead apprehend nothing. A fourth condition is knowledge, a fifth affinity, and a sixth the removal of obstacles. Thus the human being, insofar as he is human, [cannot apprehend that in which] there is no multiplicity at all, for the reason already given. He apprehends the Real only in respect of His attributes or loci of manifestation.

If it is asked, ‘Does this not contradict the earlier account of essential self-disclosure to him?’ we answer: this self-disclosure does not occur while his egoity remains, but when it is overwhelmed beneath the light of the unitary self-disclosure and existential unity predominates over him in that soul. There is an oneness within the human being: when it appears and predominates, he apprehends through it, not through his humanity. Yet the human being in respect of his oneness apprehends nothing. If he apprehends, he no longer remains a human being qualified by oneness. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “Let us return to complete the discussion we were pursuing. We say: in the case of the Real, existence is His very Essence; in everything other than Him it is something additional to its reality. The reality of each existent is the relation of its determination in its Lord's knowledge from eternity. In the terminology of the realized among the people of God it is called a ‘fixed entity’; in the terminology of others, a ‘quiddity,’ ‘the known nonexistent,’ ‘the established thing,’ and the like.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This returns to establishing that the Real is existence, not something additional to His reality through which—

ولذا لا يدرك الكثير بالواحد من حيث هو واحد على أنه لو أدرك الواحد بالكثير لا تنقش له صور بحسب أجزاء الكثير ، فيدرك كثيرا ، ولو أدرك الكثير بالواحد لتمثل في الواحد ، وهو محل لعدم اتساع الواحد لتمثل الكثير فيه . 
نعم يدرك الواحد بالكثير من جهة واحدة كونت الكثير بالوحدة من حيث شمول الواحد له بالقوة ؛ 

فلذلك قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ لا يدرك بسواه من حيث ما يغايره ] . 
وقال : ( من كونه واحدا ) ، ثم استشعر سواه ، لا بأنه لم يجز أن يدركه الإنسان من حيث وحدته ، فإن الكثير من حيث وحدته يجوز أن يدرك الواحد ؛ ولذلك قيد ثم المنع من حيث الكثرة ، فأجاب بأن إدراك الإنسان للحق ليس من جهة كونه واحدا وحدة حقيقية كوحدة الوجود ، 
فإنه ليس له ذلك ، سلمناه فلا ندركه إلا من حيث كثرته ، كالاتصاف بالوجود ، وفيه الكثرة من الماهية والوجود ، بل بشرط الحياة مع هذين إذ الميت لا يدرك شيئا بل بشرط رابع هو العلم ، وخامس هو المناسبة ، وسادس هو ارتفاع الموانع ، فإذا كان كذلك يقدر إدراك الإنسان من حيث هو إنسان لا كثرة فيه أصلا ، لما مر أن الكثير لا يدرك الكثير ، فلا يدرك من الحق ( إلا ) باعتبار صفاته أو مظاهره . 

فإن قيل : هذا يناقض ما مر من التجلي الذاتي له ، قلنا : ليس ذلك التجلي مع بقاء أنانيته بل مع صيرورتها مغلوبة تحت نور التجلي الأحدي  “ 1  “ ، وغلبة الوحدة الوجودية عليه في تلك النفس ، وفي الإنسان أحدية إذا ظهرت وغلبت أدرك بها لا من حيث إنسانيته ، لكن الإنسان من حيث أحديته لا يدرك شيئا ، فإن أدرك فلا يبقى إنسانا موصوفا بالأحدية ، فافهم . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ ثم نرجع إلى تمام ما كنا بسبيله ، فنقول : الوجود في حق الحق عين ذاته فيما عداه أمر زائد على حقيقته ، وحقيقة كل موجود عبارة عن نسبة تعينه في علم ربه أزلا ، ويسمى باصطلاح المحققين من أهل اللّه عينا ثابتة ، وباصطلاح غيرهم ماهية ، والمعلوم المعدوم والشيء الثابت ونحو ذلك ] . 

رجوع إلى تحقيق كون الحق هو الوجود ، لا أمر زائد على حقيقته يتقوم بذلك

patches.title: Human conditions of knowledge and the return to the fixed entities

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —it would subsist by that existence, and without its accession would not exist but remain nonexistent. As for the first claim: if His existence subsisted in His quiddity, it would need that quiddity, which would be other than it; whatever needs another is possible. The [cause] cannot be other than the quiddity, or His existence would be necessary through another. It must therefore be the quiddity. A cause precedes its effect in existence; the quiddity would thus precede existence through existence. This is impossible and contradictory, entailing a thing's preceding itself and an infinite regress.

It may be said: the cause precedes, but we deny that it must precede in existence. Consider a possible quiddity: it receives existence, and the recipient precedes, though not through existence, as you yourselves have said. Again, parts constitute a composite quiddity; what constitutes precedes, but not through existence, since we affirm this priority even when we disregard existence.

We answer: the intellect must first consider existence in that which imparts existence, and must consider the absence of existence in that which receives it. In what constitutes a quiddity, it must disregard both existence and nonexistence. The objection is therefore removed. The difference between the disputed case and your examples is clear: existence is considered in the disputed case, nonexistence in the first example, and neither in the second.

If you say, ‘We do not grant that what imparts existence to something must possess existence beforehand; this applies only when it imparts existence to another, or else it would exist twice,’ we answer: existence would then be other than the quiddity that brings it into existence. That quiddity would have an existence before its existence, and there would be an infinite regress. Moreover, we do not grant that the parts of a quiddity lack priority in mind and externally.

As for the second claim, there are several arguments. First: a possible quiddity, considered as such, admits nonexistence; otherwise possibility would disappear. The quiddity together with existence refuses nonexistence. If existence were the quiddity itself or a part of it, the quiddity could not admit nonexistence, because contradictories would coexist. Rather, in itself it would refuse nonexistence, just as it does when existence is considered.

It may be said: if by admitting nonexistence you mean that it is established while devoid of existence, we do not grant its establishment then. If you mean its cessation, we do not grant that, were it existence, it could not admit cessation. Existence itself ceases; thus existence admits nonexistence without contradictories coexisting.

We answer: its establishment is necessary, because it is not made, as he will shortly explain. We deny that existence ceases; otherwise it would receive its contradictory, which is even more impossible than the coexistence of contradictories, as already stated. Second: we conceive a quiddity while doubting its existence.

It may be said: its external existence, not its mental existence, which is the very act of conception; the discussion concerns existence without qualification.

الوجود ، وإن لم يلحقها لم توجد بل بقيت معدومة أما الأول ؛ فلأنه لو قام وجوده بماهيته ، لكان محتاجا إليها وهي غيره ، والمحتاج إلى الغير ممكن ، وهي ليست غير الماهية ، وإلا لكان وجوده الواجب بغيره ، فهي الماهية ، والعلة متقدمة على المعلول بالوجود ، فتتقدم الماهية على الوجود بالوجود ، وأنه محال ومتناقض ، ولازمة تقدم الشيء على نفسه والتسلسل . 
قيل : العلة متقدمة إما بالوجود ، فممنوع كتقدم الماهية الممكنة فإنها قابلة للوجود والقابل يتقدم لا بالوجود ، كما ذكرتم بعينه ، وأيضا فالأجزاء مقومة للماهية المركبة ، والمقومة متقدم وليس بالوجود ؛ لأنّا نجزم بذلك التقدم ، وإن قطعنا النظر عن الوجود . 

قلنا : المفيد للوجود لا بد ، وأن يلحظ العقل له وجود أولا ، والمستفيد للوجود لا بد ، وأن يلحظ له الخلو عن الوجود والمقوم للماهية يجب أن يقطع فيه النظر عن وجوده وعدمه ، فالمنع مندفع والفرق بين صورة النزاع ، وما جعلتموه سندا بيّن لصورة الوجود في صورة النزاع ، والعدم في السند الأولى وقطع النظر في الثاني لضرورة . 
فإن قلت : لا نسلم أن المفيد ، وجود لشيء لا بدّ وأن يكون له وجود قبله ، وإنما هو لو أفاد لغيره لا غير ، وإلا لزم كونه موجودا مرتين . 

قلنا : الوجود حينئذ غير الماهية الموجدة ، فيكون لها وجود قبل وجودها ويتسلسل ، على أنا لا نسلم أن أجزاء الماهية ليست متقدمة ذهنا وخارجا . 
وأما الثاني فلوجوه : الأول : الماهية الممكنة من حيث هي تقبل العدم ، وإلا ارتفع الإمكان والماهية مع الوجود تأباه ، ولو كان نفس الماهية أو جزؤها لم تكن قابلة للعدم لاجتماع النقيضين ، بل كانت تأبى العدم من حيث هي هي ، كما تأباه مع اعتبار الوجود . 
قيل : إن أردت بقبولها العدم ، إنها تثبت خالية عن الوجود ، فلا نسلم ثبوتها حينئذ ، وإن أردت ارتفاعها ، فلا نسلم أنها لو كانت الوجود لما قبلته ، لأن الوجود نفسه يرتفع ، فالوجود يقبل العدم ، ولا يلزم اجتماع النقيضين . 

قلنا ثبوتها ضروري ؛ لأنها غير مجعولة على ما يذكره آنفا ، وارتفاع الوجود ممنوع ، وإلا لكان قابلا لنقيضه ، وهو أشد من اجتماع النقيضين على ما مر ، الثاني : إنّا نعقل الماهية مع الشك في وجودها . 
قيل : في الخارجي دون الذهني ، فإنه نفس التعقل ، والكلام في الوجود المطلق .

patches.title: Arguments for existence as the Real’s Essence and as additional to contingent quiddities

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** The answer is that the realization of mental existence does not prevent doubt about it. Hence people have disagreed about it, and whoever establishes it does so by demonstration. Moreover, an external quiddity is devoid of mental existence until it is conceived, so the two differ. Its difference from external existence has already been established; it therefore differs from existence without qualification. There are lengthy investigations here, most of which were treated in the introduction. What remains is not appropriate to the books of the Sufis; consult works of theology and philosophy for it.

He then states what the reality of each thing is—the reality to which existence is additional: the relation of its determination in its Lord's knowledge from eternity.

To explain: the eternal Essence includes many affairs, without distinction among them within it. Eternal knowledge has a relation to each affair, through which it becomes determined and a form in eternal knowledge. Through the attribution of existence to it, the thing is realized. Hence the theologians say that every thing has a reality through which it is what it is, different from everything else, whether inseparable from it or separable. That reality answers the question ‘What is it?’—for example, ‘rational animal’ in answer to ‘What is a human being?’

The words ‘the relation of its determination’ exclude the affairs and absolute existence, in which there is no relation. ‘In the knowledge of the Real’ excludes their appearance in the forms of existence, for these are existent quiddities. It also excludes [creaturely] knowledge: quiddities need not be established there except in accordance with the Real's knowledge. In creatures' knowledge they are conceptual matters whose establishment is not necessary. Hence the theologians say that they are not established apart from existence. ‘From eternity’ excludes the Real's knowledge of them as qualified by existence in His knowledge, for that qualification is not the quiddity itself but additional to it, as we have said.

In the terminology of the people of God, who make this reality an established, eternal matter, it is called an ‘entity’ because of its determination and distinction, and ‘fixed’ because of its establishment in the knowledge of the Real, without qualification by external existence. In the terminology of others it is a ‘quiddity,’ because for them the thing is realized through it; for the realized knowers, however, realization is through existence, not through it. ‘The known nonexistent’ is the expression of some theologians who hold that existence is additional to it: for them it is not established and is therefore nonexistent. ‘The established thing’ is the expression of the majority of the Muʿtazila, on the basis that the possible nonexistent is established. For the people of God, however, ‘thing’ is restricted to the existent, because He says, ‘I created you before, when you were not a thing’ [Q 19:9], although you were possible. Here there are—

أجيب : بأن تحقق الذهني لا يمنع الشك فيه ؛ ولذلك اختلف فيه ، فمن أثبته فالبرهان ، وأيضا فالماهية الخارجية خالية عن الوجود الذّهني ما لم يتعقل ، فتغايرتان .
وقد ثبتت مغايرة الخارجي لها فتغاير المطلق ، لا وهاهنا أبحاث طويلة مر أكثرها في المقدمة ، ولا يليق ما بقي منها بكتب الصوفية ، فليراجع بها كتب الكلام والحكمة .
ثم ذكر رضي اللّه عنه ما هو حقيقة كل شيء ، وهي التي يزيد عليها الوجود ، بأنها عبارة عن نسبة تعينه في علم ربه أزلا .

بيانه : إن الذات الأزلية مشتملة على شؤون كثيرة لا تميز لها فيها ، وللعلم الأزلي نسبة إلى كل شأن ، بها يتعين ويصير صورة في العلم الأزلي ، وبإضافة الوجود إليها يتحقق الشيء .
فلذا قال المتكلمون : لكل شيء حقيقة هي بها ، هي مغايرة لما عداه لازما أو مفارقا ، فيجاب بها عند السؤال بما هو كالحيوان الناطق في جواب :  “ ما الإنسان  “ .
فمعنى قوله : عن نسبة تعينه احتراز عن الشؤون ، وعن الوجود المطلق الذي لا نسبة فيه .

وقوله :  “ في علم الحق  “ احتراز عن ظهورها بصور الوجود ، فإنها ماهيات موجودة .
واحترز بذلك أيضا عن علم الحق ، فإن الماهيات لا يجب ثبوتها فيه إلا بحسب علم الحق ، وفي علم الخلق ، هي أمور اعتبارية لا يجب ثبوتها .
فلذلك قال المتكلمون : هي لا تثبت مجردة عن الوجود ، وقوله : أزلا ، احتراز عن علم الحق بها في علمه تعالى متصفة بالوجود ، فإن ذلك ليس من نفس الماهية بل زائدا عليها كما ذكرنا . وتسمى هذه الحقيقة باصطلاح أهل اللّه الجاعلين لها أمرا ثابتا أزليّا علنيّا لتعينها وتميزها ثابتة لثبوتها في علم الحق ، من غير اتصاف بالوجود الخارجي .

وباصطلاح غيرهم إما ماهية ؛ لأن تحقق الشيء بهذا عندهم ، وأما عند المحققين فبالوجود لا بها ، وأما المعلوم والمعدوم قول بعض المتكلمين القائلين بزيادة الوجود عليها ، وهي عندهم غير ثابتة فهي معدومة ، وأما الشيء الثابت ، وهو قول جمهور المعتزلة بقاء على أن المعدوم الممكن ثابت ، لكن الشيء عند أهل اللّه يختص بالموجود ، لقوله :

patches.title: The eternal determination of realities and competing terms for quiddity

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —lengthy investigations that do not concern our present subject.

**Qūnawī:** “From the Real—glory be to Him—in respect of the unity of His existence, only one proceeds. For it is impossible for the one, insofar as it is one, to manifest and bring into existence what is more than one. For us, however, that one is the general existence effused upon the entities of generated things: those that have come to exist and those that have not, whose existence was previously known. This existence is common to the Supreme Pen, which is the first existent and is also called the First Intellect, and to all other existents, as the speculative philosophers have mentioned. For the realized knowers, there is nothing but the Real and the world. The world is nothing additional to realities known to God—as we indicated before—qualified by existence as established.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Having finished explaining that He is existence itself, he begins what follows from its unity. He says that in respect of the unity of His existence only one proceeds from Him, because of the necessary impossibility of the one, insofar as it is one, manifesting more than one. The same applies to the one bringing more than one into existence insofar as it is one.

The realized master Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī—may God sanctify his secret—said:

“This judgment is close to evident. People's frequent resistance to it is due to their overlooking the meaning of true unity. Its demonstration is this: the concept of a thing's being such that A necessarily follows from it differs from the concept of its being such that B necessarily follows from it. That is, its causality for one differs from its causality for the other. The difference between the two concepts indicates a difference between their realities. Thus what was supposed to be one thing is two things, or a thing described by two differing attributes, although we supposed it one. This is a contradiction. This much suffices to establish the point.”

He then adds, for greater clarity:

“If two necessarily follow from the one, they are either its constituents, its concomitants, or one is a constituent and the other a concomitant. If we suppose them to be concomitants, the original argument returns unchanged: its being such that the first reality necessarily follows differs from its being such that the second necessarily follows. [The printed transition to their being constituents is compressed.] If we suppose the third case, the respect entailing that concomitant must be the same respect as that constituent. The principle of the respect of entailment must not lie outside its essence, or else the argument returns. In each case composition follows: either in the structure of the thing, as with a body divided into matter—”

patches.title: The one effect and al-Ṭūsī’s argument for the principle of unity

patches.en:
**Al-Ṭūsī, quoted by al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** “—and form; or because it exists after being a certain thing, as with the First Intellect, through the multiplicity that necessarily accompanies its existence owing to the difference between its quiddity and its existence; or after its existence through division, as with a thing divided into its parts or its particulars. In every case its reality is divisible.” Here his words end—may his station be exalted.

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** If you say, ‘This argument entails that a simple thing cannot cause even one effect. The concept of its being the agent of such-and-such differs from the concept of its essence: we conceive the simple essence while doubting whether it causes such-and-such. If this concept constitutes it, it is composite; if it is a concomitant, the argument begins anew. There is no infinite regress, but an ultimate constitutive respect, and thus composition follows.

‘In sum, this regress follows not from a plurality of effects but from the causal respect's difference from the essence, and from its being caused by the essence if it is not constitutive. Whether it causes one or more makes no difference. One must therefore accept the regress or hold that this respect is uncaused. Either way, the argument fails.’

I answer: the single respect is His Essence; this cannot hold of two different respects. It is therefore neither caused nor constitutive, and may be a cause, so the two respects would not be different. [The printed text repeats this last reasoning; its wording is unstable.]

If you say, ‘We do not grant the necessity of a regress. It would follow only if being a cause were a positive matter; this is denied, for it is another, eternal matter, and it requires a cause [as printed].’

I answer: its being an entailing cause is a positive matter, because the existence of the effect depends on it. Unless the agent is in itself such that the effect necessarily follows from it, the effect does not proceed. Not everything is an agent of everything. There must be a meaning peculiar to it, in respect of which it is an agent, whether anyone considers it or not.

If you say, ‘If its being a cause is conceptual, the argument falls; if real, two have proceeded from the First, since the first effect would not be an effect.’ I answer: the First Principle is a cause through itself, so its causality is its very Essence. Otherwise the effect would depend on another matter that makes its existence from Him preponderate. That matter would then be the first effect, a contradiction.

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī, reporting al-Rāzī (continuing):** —those things of it, its qualification by them, and its reception of them differ. The division just given returns, until it follows that only one thing can be denied of the one insofar as it is one, that it can be qualified by only one thing, and that it can receive only one thing.

**Al-Ṭūsī, quoted in reply:** “Denying one thing of another, one thing's qualification by another, and one thing's reception of another are matters not realized by the existence of just one thing. They do not follow from the one insofar as it is one, but require more than one antecedent thing, so that these matters follow for those things under differing considerations. The proceeding of many things from many things is not impossible.

“To explain: negation requires the prior establishment of both what is negated and that of which it is negated; the latter's establishment alone does not suffice. Qualification likewise requires a qualified subject and an attribute, and receptivity a recipient and something received. Difference in what is received, such as blackness and motion, requires a difference in the recipient's condition. A body receives blackness insofar as it is affected by another, and receives motion insofar as it has a condition that does not [prevent] its departure from it. But for the proceeding of one thing from another it suffices to posit a single thing, the cause. Otherwise it would be impossible for all effects to depend upon one principle.

“Do not say that proceeding, too, is realized only after both a source and something proceeding are realized. We answer: ‘proceeding’ has two meanings. One is a relation accruing to cause and effect insofar as both are together; this is not our subject. The second is the cause's being such that an effect proceeds from it. In this sense it precedes the effect and then the relation accruing to both. This is our subject. It is one matter if the effect is one. That matter may be the very essence of the cause, if the cause causes through itself. Or it may be a state accruing to the cause, if it causes not through itself but according to another state. If the effects are more than one, that matter must differ, and multiplicity within the essence of the cause follows, as already stated.” End of quotation.

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** It has also been objected that bringing into existence is impossible without two things proceeding: quiddity and existence. Again, the central point stands in relation to [many] points; the concept of its being opposite one point differs from the concept of its being opposite—

patches.title: Al-Ṭūsī’s reply: negation, reception, and two senses of proceeding

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —another. If one or both of these [relations] were intrinsic to the central point, composition in it would follow. Otherwise the point would be their source, and either composition or an infinite regress would follow. Again, substantiality causes spatial occupancy and the reception of existent accidents: two effects of something simple. Do not say that one is in respect of a state and the other in respect of a place, for our discussion concerns its receptivity to both, which is among the accidents of its essence.

The answer is that quiddity is not made. Even if we grant that it is made, it is described as preceding existence, which is its attribute. Do not say that making it is precisely obtaining its existence; we answer that then the quiddity is not made. It remains as it was, but has been qualified by existence.

The central point's being opposite a point on the circumference is in respect of the relation between them; this differs from the relation between it and another point on the circumference. The two oppositions therefore do not arise from one aspect. The cause of each relation is the central point together with a point on the circumference. The argument about substance is complete only if its simplicity is established, both matters are established as existent, and the plurality of grounds and conditions is excluded: it receives spatial occupancy because it has position, and accidents because it is a substrate.

It may be said: if only one proceeds from the one, [one would produce one other], and so on to the last of existents. This is false: Zayd is plainly not the cause of ʿAmr, nor vice versa. Al-Ṭūsī answers in his treatise: more than one may proceed from the one when it is not considered [in isolation from] something else. For example, when one other proceeds from the one, another, B, may proceed from the two together; then another, C, from it together with B; then one other from every pair. Thus it does not follow that either of two things is the cause of the other: one may belong to one chain and the other to another.

It may be said: if one proceeds from Him and then another from Him together with the first, His effect upon the first is unconditional, while His effect upon the second is conditional upon the first. Being the source of the first unconditionally differs from being the source of the second conditionally; either composition or an infinite regress follows. We answer: we do not grant that the First alone acts upon the third. What acts is the aggregate, and the composition is in that aggregate.

لأخرى ، فإن كان أحدهما أو كلاهما داخلا في النقطة المركزية لزم تركيبها ، وإلا لا تكون النقطة مصدرا لهما ، وللزم إما التركيب أو التسلسل ، وأيضا الجوهرية علة للتحيز والقبول للأعراض الوجودية ، فهما أثران لبسيط . 
لا يقال : أحدهما باعتبار الحال ، والآخر باعتبار الحيز ؛ لأنّا نقول الكلام في قابليته لهما ، وهو من عوارض ذاته . 
والجواب : أن الماهية غير مجعولة ، ولو سلمنا أنها مجعولة ، فهي موصوفة بتقدم على الوجود الذي هو صفتها . 

لا يقال : جعلها عين تحصيل وجودها ، لأنا نقول : فليست الماهية مجعولة بل هي مستقرة على ما كانت لكنها وصفت بالوجود ، ومحاذاة نقطة المركز لنقطة من المحيط باعتبار ما بينهما من النسبة ، وهي غير النسبة التي بينهما وبين أخرى من المحيط ، فليس المحاذاتان من جهة واحدة ، وعلة كل نسبة نقطة المركز مع نقطة من المحيط ، وكون الجوهر لها إنما يتم ببيان بساطته ، وكون الأمرين وجودين ، وانتفاء تعدد الأدلة والشرط على قبول التحيز ، لكونه إذا وضع ، وللأعراض لكونه محلا . 

قيل : لو لم يصدر عن الواحد إلا الواحد يلزم أن لا يوجد الواحد واحدا آخر ، وعلى هذا إلى آخر الموجودات ، وذلك باطل ، ضرورة أن زيدا ليس علة عمرو وبالعكس . 
وأجاب عنه الطوسي في رسالته : إن الواحد الذي لا أعتبر معه شيئا آخر ، جاز أن يصدر عنه أكثر من واحد ، مثلا إذا صدر عن الواحد واحدا آخر ، يجوز أن يصدر مع واحد آخر - كب - وعنه مع - ب - آخر ( كج ) ، ثم مع كل اثنين واحد آخر ، وعلى هذا فلا يلزم كون كل واحد من الشيئين على الآخر لجواز أن يكون أحدهما من سلسلة ، والآخر من سلسلة أخرى . 

قيل : لو صدر عنه واحد ، ثم معه آخر له تأثير في الأول بلا شرط ، وفي الثانية بشرط الأول ، فكونه للأول بلا شرط غير كونه مصدرا للثاني بالشرط ، ويلزم إما التركيب والتسلسل . 

قلنا : لا نسلم أن الأول مؤثر في الثالث ، بل المؤثر هو المجموع والتركيب فيه . 
على أنّا نقول ، إنما يلزم أن يكون أحد الشيئين علة للآخر ، إن كان المعلول الأول

**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —were one existent in every respect. But the effect must have an existence proceeding from the Necessary, and a quiddity receiving it through possibility. Something else may therefore proceed from the first effect in respect of each constituent.

Once you know this, we say that the author mentioned the impossibility of the one ‘manifesting’ [more than one] so that one should not suppose the prohibition to concern only origination and to exclude the Sufis' account of things as manifestations. He included this to make the generality explicit. [The printed sentence is defective.]

The view that more than one cannot proceed from what is one in every respect is subject to the scholars' denunciation because it entails things interposed between the Real and daily occurrences and other things, in such a way that He would be unable to originate them without [these intermediaries; the printed transition is defective]. For this reason they declared the philosophers who hold it unbelievers. The shaykh rejects what entails that consequence while accepting the principle. He says: for us that one is general, absolute, simple existence. Its multiplicity does not contradict its true unity; likewise the relations and subtle connections in the First Intellect.

This existence is effused upon all the entities of possible things and their realities fixed in eternal knowledge. [The printed wording that follows, beginning فأبعد منها في الحال والماضي لم توجد, is corrupt.] It speaks of what has not existed in the present or past, of impossibility even when through another, and of eternal foreknowledge that it will not exist. Yet eternal knowledge concerns the existence of things. General existence is connected with them potentially from eternity, while their actual manifestation follows the order. Knowledge concerns each thing according to what it is.

This general existence is common to the Supreme Pen, which is the first existent through that general existence, as the report says, ‘The first thing God created was the Pen.’ It is also called the First Intellect, in the saying attributed here to the Prophet, ‘The first thing God created was the Intellect.’ It is called a pen because it is the principle of recording and writing, and an intellect because it is immaterial. This existence is also common to all the other existents, even daily occurrences, so that all depend upon God without an intermediary. His effect is not confined to the First Intellect, as the speculative philosophers say.

He qualifies them as the speculative philosophers because the other theologians, apart from the Muʿtazila, reject both the consequence and the principle—

موجودا واحدا من جميع الوجوه ، فإن المعلول لا بدّ من وجود صدر عن الواجب ، وماهية يقبله من إمكان ، فيجوز أن يصدر من المعلول الأول لكل جزء وشيء آخر . 
وإذا عرفت هذا ، 

فنقول : إنما قال المصنف رضي اللّه عنه :  “ لا استحالة إظهار الواحد ؛ لئلا يتوهم أن الواحد إنما يمتنع عنه صدور الواحد ، لإظهاره عن مذهب الصوفية في الأشياء ، فأشار إليه ليفهم العموم صريحا ، ثم لما كان هذا المذهب إلى امتناع صدور أكثر من واحد ، من الواحد من كل الوجوه محل تشنيع العلماء ؛ 

لاستلزامه وجود الأشياء المتوسطة بين الحق والحوادث اليومية ، وغيرها بحيث يعجز عن إيجاد بدون مشرب هذه الطائفة ، 
فلذلك كفّروا القائلين به من الفلاسفة ، منع الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه ما يستلزم ذلك من قبول الأصل ، فقال : لكن ذلك الواحد عندنا هو الوجود العالم المطلق البسيط ، وتكثره لا ينافي وحدته الحقيقية ، 
كذلك النسب والرقائق في العقل الأول ، فهذا الوجود فاض على جميع أعيان الممكنات ، والحقائق الثابتة لها في العلم الأزلي ، فأبعد منها في الحال والماضي لم توجد ، فإنه محال وإن كان بالغير ، وقد سبق العلم الأزلي بأنه لا يوجد ، ولكن العلم الأزلي يتعلق بوجود الأشياء ، وكذلك تعلق بذلك الوجود العام في الأزل بالقوة ، ولكن ظهورها بالفعل تابع للنظام ، ويتعلق العلم بكل شيء وعلى ما هو عليه . 

وهذا الوجود العام مشترك بين القلم الأعلى الذي هو أول موجود بذلك الوجود العام ، كما ورد في الحديث :  “ أول ما خلق اللّه القلم  “  “ 1  “ . 
وهو المسمى بالعقل الأول ، حيث قال صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ أول ما خلق اللّه العقل  “  “ 2  “ ، وسمي قلما ؛ لأنه مبدأ التدوين والتسطير . 
وعقلا بكونه مجردا ، ولبيان سائر الموجودات حتى الحوادث اليومية حتى يستند الجميع إلى اللّه تعالى بلا واسطة وليس معلوله عزّ وجلّ منحصرا فيه ، كما يقوله أهل النظر من الفلاسفة  “ 3  “ .

patches.title: General existence and the rejection of compulsory intermediaries

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —because in their view both necessarily entail an intermediary between Him and all other existents. The shaykh then rejects this intermediary because it would be between a thing and itself: in reality there is only the Real. The world is nothing additional to realities known to God. Initially they have nothing in existence apart from their establishment in His knowledge; then they are qualified by external existence. An intermediary would therefore be either between Him and His existence, which is His very self; between Him and other realities; or between Him and the aggregate of the world's existence and its realities.

He indicates the invalidity of the second possibility as follows:

**Qūnawī:** “The realities, in respect of their being known and the determination of their forms in the Real's essential, eternal knowledge, cannot be made: originated things cannot subsist in the Essence of the Real, and the Real cannot be a container for another or be contained. There are other corrupt consequences that are evident to those with insight. Understand.

“For this reason they are not described as made by realized people of unveiling, or by realized speculative thinkers. What is made is existence; what has no existence is not made. If it were otherwise, eternal knowledge would have an effect upon the determination of its objects within it from eternity, although they are not external to the one who knows them. To affirm that they are made would therefore require either their co-presence in existence with their knower, or that their knower be a locus receiving an effect from himself within himself, and also a container for another, as stated. All this is false, for it impugns the purity of His unity and entails that effused existence accrues as an accident to already existent things, not nonexistent ones. All this is impossible, because it obtains what is already obtained, and for other reasons there is no need to discuss at length. Understand.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** It is thus established that in the respect mentioned they are not made. There are not two existences, as we have said: existence is one, common to all of them and received from the Real. An intermediary between the Real and the realities of the world could be conceived only if those realities were made. But in respect of their being known to the Real—the determination of their forms in His essential, eternal knowledge—they cannot be made. The realities are realized in this respect, apart from existence, before the world. This respect has therefore belonged to them from eternity and is everlasting.

In respect of their being forms known to someone other than God, or known to Him through the manifestation of His knowledge in loci of manifestation, they may be made; but this is an incidental matter. Insofar as they are realities, they are not made. Their being made in the former respect is impossible because that knowledge does not differ from the Essence in any way. It shares the Essence's immunity from originated things subsisting within it. Moreover, what subsists in that knowledge, an attribute of the Real, subsists in the Real. If—

ثم إن الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه منع هذه الواسطة بأنها بين الشيء ونفسه ، إذ ليس في الواقع إلا الحق ، إذ العالم ليس بشيء زائد على حقائق معلومة للّه تعالى ،

patches.title: Why the fixed realities are not made in eternal knowledge

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —they were made, they would be originated, and could not subsist in the Essence of the Real or in His inseparable, eternal attribute. If those realities did not subsist in the Real or in knowledge while being established there, they would either inhere [in Him] or be substrates for Him, and all of this is impossible. To make them made also entails other corrupt consequences evident to those with insight. For these reasons realized people of unveiling, and realized speculative philosophers, do not describe them as made.

He then explains those corrupt consequences, after indicating that they are so clear that every realized knower accepts them: what is made is external existence, and what is not external is not made. The entities have no existence, even though existence appears through them, upon them, and is attributed to them.

Moreover, if quiddities were made—and there is no doubt that they are known to God, since His eternal knowledge encompasses all—they would first have originated in His eternal knowledge. They would not originate from the Essence as such, because of its independence of everything. Eternal knowledge would therefore have an effect upon the determination of its objects within it, although its objects are not external to their knower: they subsist in the knowledge that subsists in Him. Rather, they are nonexistent for themselves and have no existence except through the Real, since He is absolute existence. Their existence is not external, so it could only be within the essence of their knower.

If their being made were affirmed, they would either be originated from eternity, co-present in existence with their knower—but temporal origination from eternity is impossible—or not co-present, but originated within His Essence. Their knower would then either be His very self, making Him a locus receiving an effect from Himself in Himself, or be other than Him, making Him a container for another. He transcends being a container or something contained.

He then invalidates all of this by an argument suited to divine unity: God is one in every respect in His eternity. This would impugn the purity of His unity, since differing realities would exist alongside Him with independent existence [the following printed transition is unclear]. Furthermore, if they were made, they would be existent; existence effused upon them would then be an accident of things already existent. Existence would be repeated upon them: obtaining what is already obtained. This is impossible for that reason and for others that need not be discussed at length.

For example: the quiddities would then be realized by existence while it was absent. Or: if they were made, humanity would, when not made, be [not] humanity. It would therefore be denied of itself, which is—

كانت مجعولة لكانت حادثة ، فيمتنع قيامها بذات الحق وصفته اللازمة القديمة أيضا . 
فإن لم تكن تلك الحقائق قائمة بالحق ، ولا يعلم وهي ثابتة هناك ، فهي إما حالة أو محال له ، والكل محال ، على أن في جعلها مجعولة ، مفاسد أخرى لا تخفى على المستبصر ، وتلك المفاسد لا توصف بالجعل عند المحققين من أهل الكشف ، ومن أهل النظر من الحكماء أيضا . 

ثم بيّن تلك المفاسد بعد الإشارة إلى كونها في غاية الوضوح بحيث يسلمها كل محقق بأن المجعول هو الوجود الخارجي ، فما لا يكون في الخارج لا يكون مجعولا ، والأعيان لا وجود لها وإن ظهر بها الوجود ، وظهر عليها وأضيف إليها . 

وأيضا لو كانت الماهيات مجعولة ، ولا شك أنها معلومات للحق تعالى لشمول علمه الأزلي على الكل ، لكان أول حدثت في علمه الأزلي ، ولم يوجد عن الذات من حيث هي ؛ لغنائها عن الكل ، فكان للعلم القديم أثر في تعين معلوماته فيه ، مع أن المعلومات غير خارجة عن العالم بها ؛ لأنها قائمة بالعلم القائم به ، بل هي قائمة ؛ لأنها معدومة لأنفسها ، فلا وجود لها إلا بالحق إذ هو الوجود المطلق ووجودها ليس في الخارج ، فلا يكون إلا في ذات العالم بها . 

فلو قيل بجعلها ، فإما أن تكون حادثة في الأزل مساوقة للعالم بها في الوجود ، لكن الحدوث الزمني في الأزل محال ، أولا مساوقة لكنها حادثة في ذاته ، فالعالم بها إما عينه ، فيكون محلا لقبول الأثر من نفسه في نفسه ، أو غيره فيكون ظرفا لغيره ، وتعالى أن يكون ظرفا أو مظروفا . 

ثم أبطل الكل بدليل تناسب التوحيد بأنه تعالى واحد من كل وجه من حيث أزليته ، وهذا قادح في صرافة وحدته إذ الحقائق المختلفة موجودة معه بوجود مستقل ، فلا يكون إلا بالترتيب معه على أنها لو كانت مجعولة ، لكانت موجودة والوجود الفائض عليها يكون عرضا لها ، وهي موجودة فيتكرر الوجود عليها ، فهو تحصيل الحاصل ، فهو محال من هذا الوجه ، ومن وجوه أخر لا حاجة إلى التطويل بها . 

مثل ما يقال : الماهيات حينئذ إنما تتحقق بالوجود حال عدمه ، مثل ما يقال ، لو كانت مجعولة ، لكانت الإنسانية عند عدم جعلها الإنسانية ، فيلزم سلبه عن نفسه ، وهو
