patches.title: Permeation without division or indwelling

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —otherwise originated things would be eternal. It may also be said that He is receptive through Himself, but eternity prevents the reception. He thus receives the two universal rulings, detachment and restriction: detachment from everything in the first, and restriction by everything in the second. They are opposites with the utmost difference between them. Opposition, however, is considered only with respect to particular subjects and individual determinations. His receptivity is through Himself, not an additional matter ascribed to Him, since there is nothing beyond absolute existence whose attribution to Him could be considered. Although the effect of His receptivity to restriction by some matters concerns an additional matter, that matter is conceptual in relation to existence itself. His gathering of opposites—indeed, of every two differing things, whether opposed or not—is in respect of His form, not His Essence alone.

Forms differ with the different matters appearing in them, and those matters differ through the will ascribed to Him. If He wills, He appears in every form; if He does not will, no form is ascribed to Him at all. This is as on the day when He says, ‘Whose is the dominion today? God's, the One, the Overpowering’ [Q 40:16]. He says ‘if He does not will’ to indicate that willing nonexistence and not willing are alike in the non-attribution of forms. What is intended is the absence of will's connection, for will is eternal and does not cease. He then states that these forms do not change Him from what He is in oneness:

**Qūnawī:** “His determination and individuation through forms, and His qualification by their attributes, do not impair the perfection of His existence, His might, or His sanctity. His manifestation in things, His making them manifest, and His determination and restriction through them and their rulings, insofar as they are themselves, do not contradict His exaltation, freedom from restrictions, or essential independence of everything described as existent. Rather, He—glory be to Him—unites realities that resemble and differ so that they combine, and those that differ and stand apart so that they remain diverse.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** His determination through specific and individual forms, and qualification by their originated attributes, do not impair the perfection of His existence in oneness and oneness-with-multiplicity. These determinations and individuations concern the loci of manifestation, not the Essence. They therefore contradict neither the Essence's perfection, nor His might beyond connection with them, nor His sanctity beyond originated things. What happens to a form in a mirror when the mirror moves or breaks does not happen to the possessor of the form. Thus His manifestation in things, His making them manifest, His determination through their lowly ranks, and His restriction by their possible realities and originated attributes from this aspect do not contradict His exaltation from another aspect, oneness; nor His essential absoluteness—

وإلا لكانت الحوادث أزلية ، ويمكن أن يقال قابل بذاته ، إلا أن الأزل يمنع من القبول ، فهذا قابل لهذين الحكمين التجرد والتقيد الكليين ؛ لأنه اعتبر التجرد عن الكل في الأول ، والتقيد بالكل في الثاني ، وهما متضادان ، بينهما غاية الخلاف إلا أن الضدية إنما تعتبر بالنظر إلى الموضوعات الخاصة والتعينات الشخصية ، وقبوله له بذاته لا بأمر زائد ينضاف إليه إذ ليس وراء الوجود المطلق شيء حتى يعتبر انضيافه إليه ، وإن كان أثر قابليته للتقيد ببعض الأمور باعتبار الأمر الزائد ، لكن ذلك الأمر اعتباري بالنظر إلى نفس الوجود . نعم جمعيته المتقابلين ، بل لكل مختلفين سواء كان بينهما تقابل أم لا ، باعتبار صورته لا باعتبار ذاته فقط . 

واختلاف الصور باختلاف ما ظهر فيها من الأمور المختلفة ، واختلاف تلك الأمور بما ينضاف إليه من المشيئة ، فإذا شاء ظهر في كل صورة ، وإن لم يشأ لا ينضاف إليه صورة أصلا ، كما يكون يوم يقول عز وجل :لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْواحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ[ غافر : 16 ] . 
وإنما قال : وإن لم يشأ ؛ ليشعر بأن مشيئة العدم ، وعدم المشيئة سواء في عدم انضياف الصور ، والمراد عدم تعلق المشيئة ، وإلا فالمشيئة قديمة لا تنعدم ، ثم ذكر أن هذه الصور لا تغيره عما كان عليه في الأحدية . 

فذلك قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ لا يقدح تعينه وتشخصه بالصور ، واتصافه بصفاتها في كمال وجوده وعزه وقدسه ، ولا ينافي ظهوره في الأشياء وإظهاره وتعينه وتقيده بها وبأحكامها من حيث هي علوه وإطلاقه من القيود وغناه بذاته عن جميع ما وصف بالوجود ، بل هو سبحانه الجامع بين ما تماثل من الحقائق وتخالف فيتألف ، وبين ما تغاير وتباين فيختلف ] . 

أي : لا يقدح تعينه بالصور النوعية والشخصية ، واتصافه بصفاته الحادثة في كمال وجوده الأحدية والواحدية ؛ لأن هذه التعيّنات والتشخّصات باعتبار المظاهر لا بالذات ، فلا ينافي كمال الذات ولا عزته عن التعلق بها ، ولا قدسه عن الحوادث لذلك ، فإن ما يلحق الصورة في المرآة عند تحريكها أو كسرها ، لا يلحق شيء ذا الصورة ، ولذلك لا ينافي ظهوره في الأشياء ، وإظهاره للأشياء ولا تعينه بمراتبها الدنيّة ، ولا تقيده بحقائقها الممكنة وبصفاتها الحادثة من هذه الحيثية ، علوه من حيثية أخرى هي الأحدية ، ولا إطلاقه الذاتي

patches.title: Opposing rulings and forms that do not alter essential perfection

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —nor His essential independence of all. Rather, while transcending all, He gathers realities that resemble one another and those that differ—that is, are proximate—and combines them. He makes them one, or gives them oneness, through the affinity between those realities, so that they accord with His unity accordingly.

He also gathers what is mutually incompatible and what stands apart, without a unifying affinity between them. They therefore do not accord with His unity and remain diverse, yet they come together through existence within existence. He does this to display receptivity through gathering and separation, because it encompasses all of them. He then mentions the names through which manifestation occurs at [origination] and concealment at annihilation:

**Qūnawī:** “Through His existential self-disclosure hidden things appear, and blessings descend from the unseen into the witnessed, through His names the Expander and the Originator. Through the withdrawal of the ruling of His descent, existents become hidden and cease, through His names the Contractor and the Restorer.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Through His self-disclosure by general existence, according to the demand of the name the Expander upon the realities, and the Originator's making it manifest as restricted by them and their states, the realities and their attributes hidden in oneness-with-multiplicity appear. The blessings of those realities descend, through manifestation, from the unseen unity into the witnessed. These are the external self-disclosures upon them, actually complete after being potentially theirs. Then, through withdrawal of the ruling of His descent—that is, His nearness to the realities—what has become actual among them in external existence becomes hidden, indeed ceases externally, according to His names the Contractor and the Expander, concerning manifestation and hiddenness, and the Restorer, who returns what appeared to what it was at first.

He then explains why these names connect with origination and annihilation:

**Qūnawī:** “He—exalted is He—was veiled by His might, and was Forgiving. When He loved to be known, He drew near and appeared in whatever He willed, however He willed, and was Loving. Through love, insofar as He is lover, He originates, and love makes Him manifest. Through love, insofar as He is lover and beloved, He restores every thing within His grasp and subdued beneath the force of His taking hold, because of the strength of His act and the weakness of what receives it.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** When He regards His exaltation and independence, He veils Himself from things through His might and is Forgiving—that is, concealing them. When He loves to be known, to perfect the world and existence through manifestation in loci and to bring what is potentially possible for both into actuality, [He draws near to] the realities and appears in whatever He wills through the eternal will that bestows preparedness upon them, however He wills there. He is thus Loving, through His appearing in them and making them appear. Through love, insofar as He is lover alone—there being no beloved from creation before origination—He originates—

ولا غناه بذاته عن الجميع ، بل هو تعالى مع تنزهه عن الجميع ، يجمع بين الحقائق المتماثلة والمتخالفة أي المتقاربة ، فيؤلّف بينهما ، فيجعلها واحدة أو أحدية بسبب المناسبة التي بين تلك الحقائق ، حتى يناسب وحدته على حسب ذلك . 

ويجمع أيضا بين ما ينافر أخرى تنافر ، وبين ما يباين ، فلا يكون بينهما مناسبة جامعة ، فلا يناسب وحدته فيختلف ، لكنها تجتمع بالوجود في الوجود . 
وإنما فعل ذلك إظهارا للقابلية على سبيل الاجتماع والافتراق ؛ لشموله لها جميعا ، ثم ذكر الأسماء التي بها الظهور عند الاتحاد والخفاء عند الإعدام . 

فلذلك قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ بتجليه الوجودي ظهرت الخفيّات ، وتنزلت من الغيب إلى الشهادة البركات ، من حيث أسمائه الباسط والمبديء ، وبارتفاع حكم تدلّيه تخفي وتنعدم الموجودات باسميه القابض والمعيد ] . 

أي : بتجليه بالوجود العام باقتضاء الاسم الباسط على الحقائق ، والمبديء إظهاره مقيدا بها وبأحوالها ، أظهرت الحقائق وأوصافها الخفيات في الواحدية ، وتنزلت بالظهور من غيب الوحدة إلى الشهادة بركات تلك الحقائق ، وهي التجليات عليها الخارجية الكاملة بالفعل بعد ما كانت لها بالقوة ، ثم بارتفاع حكم تدليه ، أي دنوه من الحقائق يخفي ما فعل منها في الوجود الخارجي ، بل ينعدم في الخارجي ، بمقتضى اسميه القابض والباسط للظهور والبطون ، والمعيد لما ظهر إلى ما كان عليه في الأول . 

ثم بيّن سبب تعلق هذه الأسماء بالإيجاد والإعدام 
بما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ إنه تعالى كان محتجبا بعزه ، فكان غفورا ، وإن أحب أن يعرف دنا وظهر فيما شاء كيف شاء ، فكان ودودا ، فبالمحبة يبدي من كونه محبّا ، وهي تبديه ، وبها من كونه محبّا ومحبوبّا يعيد كل شيء في قبضته ومقهور تحت قوة بطشه ؛ لقوة فعله وضعف المنفعل ] . 

أي : إن نظر سبحانه وتعالى علوه واستغنائه ، احتجب عن الأشياء بعزه فيكون غفورا ، أي : ساترا لها ، وإن أحب أن يعرف من جهة تكميل العالم والوجود بالظهور في المظاهر ، وإخراج ما لهما في الإمكان بالقوة إلى الفعل وما من الحقائق ، وظهر فيما شاء بالمشيئة الأزلية المفيضة عليها الاستعداد كيف شاء هناك ، فكان ودودا لظهوره فيها وإظهارها ، فبالمحبة من جهة كونه محبّا فقط ، إذ لا محبوب من الخلق قبل الإيجاد ، يبديء

patches.title: Expansion and contraction, origination and restoration through love

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —the realities by giving them existence, while love makes Him manifest by appearing in them after His manifestation through Himself within Himself. Through love, insofar as He is lover in created forms and beloved in respect of reality, He restores [them] to Himself. This includes the saying cited here as the Prophet's: ‘Love of homeland is part of faith.’

He then indicates that being lover and beloved does not suffice: every thing must also be in the grasp of His will and subdued beneath the force of His taking hold, which is His power. These are realized through the strength of His act, so that He is overpowering and grasping, and the weakness of [what receives] the act, so that it is grasped and overpowered. Thus no other is an agent, and He is not a recipient of action.

He then states what the first locus of manifestation is, through whose mediation these things and their causes appear:

**Qūnawī:** “The locus of manifestation of His power, the instrument of His wisdom in His action according to His customary way, and the locus of appearance of the secret of contraction and expansion, origination and concealment, unseen and witnessed, disclosure and the formal, causal veil through which He performs what has been mentioned—though not absolutely—is His Glorious Throne.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The locus of manifestation of His overpowering power is the Glorious Throne, which is the First Intellect, as the realized shaykh Muḥyī al-Ḥaqq wa-l-Dīn Ibn al-ʿArabī—may God sanctify his spirit—explains in his treatise called *al-ʿAqliyya*. It is an instrument for His doing things as required by the wisdom that orders effects upon their causes, according to His customary way of bringing things into existence following the orientations of the universal intellects and souls.

The First Intellect is a locus of contraction in respect of its possibility, and expansion in respect of its necessity through its Lord; origination in respect of its existence, and concealment in respect of its immateriality; unseen in respect of belonging to the world of spirits, and witnessed in respect of its manifestation through its Lord; disclosure in respect of its recording unseen matters, and a veil in respect of its mediation between the Real and creation. It thus becomes a formal veil—that is, according to outward appearance, since in reality there is no agent except God. But because things are brought into existence upon its orientation, this is attributed to it as a cause, not as an agent.

Through this, the Real does what He does on the occasion of its orientation—not through its assistance or causality, but upon its orientation. This is as we say of our acts: they are the Real's creations, yet they occur upon our orientations toward them. All are therefore His acts without qualification. He then adduces evidence for this whole account in his following statement—

الحقائق بإعطاء الوجود لها ، وتبديه بالظهور فيها بعد ظهوره بذاته في ذاته ، وبالمحبة من جهة كونه محبّا في الصور الخلقية ، ومحبوبا من جهة الحقيقة يعيد إليه ، ومنه قوله صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ حب الوطن من الإيمان  “  “ 1  “ . 

ثم أشار إلى أن المحبة والمحبوبية لا تكفيان في ذلك ، بل لا بد معها من كون كل شيء في قبضة مشيئته ، ومقهورا تحت قوة بطشه التي هو قدرته ، وهما يتمان بقوة فعله حتى يصير قاهرا قابضا ، وضعف الفعل حتى يصير مقبوضا مقهورا ؛ فلذلك لا يكون غيره فاعلا ، ولا يكون هو منفعلا . 
ثم ذكر ما هو المظهر الأول الذي بواسطته ظهرت هذه الأشياء وأسبابها 

بما قال الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه : [ ومظهر قدرته ، وآلة حكمته في فعله بسنته ، ومحل ظهور سر القبض والبسط ، والإبداء والإخفاء ، والغيب الشهادة ، والكشف والحجاب الصوري السببي الذي به يفعل ما ذكره ولا مطلقا هو عرشه المجيد ] . 
أي : مظهر قدرته القاهرة ، العرش المجيد الذي هو العقل الأول على ما فسره الشيخ المحقق المحيى الحق والدين ابن العربي قدس اللّه روحه في رسالته المسماة بـ  “ العقلية  “ ، وهو آلة لفعله الأشياء على ما اقتضته الحكمة المرتبة للمسببات على أسبابها بسنته الجارية في إيجاد الأشياء ، عقيب توجهات العقول والنفوس الكلية ؛ 

وذلك لأن العقل الأول كان محلا لظهور القبض من حيث إمكانه ، والبسط من حيث وجوبه بربه ، والإبداء مكن حيث وجوده ، والإخفاء من حيث تجرده ، والغيب من حيث كونه من عالم الأرواح والشهادة من حيث ظهوره بربه ، والكشف من حيث تسطيره لأمور الغيبية ، والحجاب من حيث توسطه بين الحق والخلق ، فصار حجابا صوريّا ، أي بحسب الظاهر إذ لا فاعل في الحقيقة إلا اللّه ، لكنه لما كان إيجاد الأشياء عند توجهه نسب إليه لكونه سببا لا لكونه فاعلا " . 

فهو الذي يفعل الحق ما يفعل بسبب توجهه لا بإعانته وسببيته ، بل عند توجهه كما نقول في أفعالنا أنها مخلوقات الحق ، لكنها توجد عند توجهاتنا إليها ؛ فلذلك كان الكل أفعاله مطلقا ، ثم استدل على هذا المجموع 

بما قال رضي اللّه عنه :

patches.title: The Glorious Throne, the First Intellect, and divine action upon causes

patches.en:
**Qūnawī (continuing):** “For this reason He—exalted is He—said, disclosing the secret of this matter: ‘For one who has a heart, or gives ear while present’ [Q 50:37]; ‘Your Lord's grasp is indeed mighty. It is He who originates and restores. He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Glorious Throne, Doer of whatever He wills’ [Q 85:12–16], in the two ranks of absoluteness and delimitation. His saying, ‘Doer of whatever He wills,’ answers an implicit question that He knew would arise from a veiled objector.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, because of the ordering we have mentioned, He—exalted is He—spoke to disclose its secret by way of allusion, so that understanding it belongs specifically to one who has a heart that discovers the obscure meanings of the Qurʾān, or who gives ear to the shaykhs who disclose them, being present and wholly attentive, as though looking at what he hears. Your Lord's “grasp”—that is, His power—is mighty: it acts upon whatever He wills, however He wills. He originates insofar as He is Loving, and restores insofar as He is both Forgiving and Loving. He does this through the Glorious Throne, which is the First Intellect. Restoration is to hiddenness; origination is to manifestation.

His saying, “Doer of whatever He wills,” indicates that He has no need of causes, as one might suppose from His saying, “Lord of the Glorious Throne.” Rather, He does whatever He wills, with causes and without them. Causes accord with wisdom. The saying also indicates that He does not necessitate things by His essence, as one might suppose from the statement that forgiveness and lovingness necessitate restoration and origination. He therefore explains that their self-disclosure, too, is through His will and choice, not through necessitation, as the people of veiling maintain.

**Text Twenty-Two**

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Having finished establishing unity, he begins to disclose what most often veils it. He explains this in his saying—may God be pleased with him—“A noble text.” It is the last of the texts because through it the clarification of divine unity, the noblest of the objects sought, attains completion. The remaining veils become easy to uncover once this is uncovered. Its position at the end is also because the complete clarification of divine unity occurs at the station of the oneness of gathering and distinction, which is the last of the stations as they are conventionally known.

**Qūnawī:** “Know that the greatest doubt and veil is that the multiplicities occurring in the one existence necessitate the effects of the fixed entities within it, and thus give the impression that the entities have appeared in existence and through existence—”
patches.ar:
[ ولهذا قال سبحانه وتعالى مبدئ سر هذا الأمر : لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ [ ق : 37 ] ، إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ ( 12 ) إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ ( 13 ) وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ ( 14 ) ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ ( 15 ) فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ ( 16 ) [ البروج : 12 - 16 ] في مرتبتي الإطلاق والتقييد ، وقوله : فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، جواب سؤال مقدر ، علم أنه يبدو من معترض محجوب]
 .
أي : لما ذكرنا من الترتيب ، قال سبحانه لإظهار سر هذا الترتيب بطريق الرمز بحيث يختص بالفهم من كان له قلب يستكشف المعاني الغامضة من القرآن ، أو ألقى السمع إلى المشايخ الكاشفة لها ، وهو حاضر كامل التوجه ، كأنه ينظر إلى ما يسمع أن بطش - أي قدرة - ربك لشديد يؤثر فيما شاء كيف شاء أنه هو يبدي من حيث كونه ودودا ، ويعيد من حيث كونه غفورا ودودا معا ، يفعل ذلك بالعرش المجيد الذي هو العقل الأول . الإعادة إلى البطون ، والإبداء إلى الظهور ، 
في قوله تعالى : فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، إشارة إلى أنه لا يحتاج إلى الأسباب كما يتوهم من قوله تعالى : ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ [ البروج : 15 ] ، بل فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، بالأسباب وبدونها . 
وإنما الأسباب على مقتضى الحكمة ، وإلى أنه ليس موجبا بالذات ، كما يتوهم من أن الغفورية والودودية يوجبان الإعادة والإبداء ، فبيّن أن تجليها أيضا بمشيئته واختياره لا بإيجاب ، كما يقول أهل الحجاب .

النص الثاني والعشرون 
ولما فرغ عن تحقيق التوحد ، شرع في كشف ما يحجب عنه غالبا ، فذلك بما قال رضي اللّه عنه :
[ نص شريف ] هو آخر النصوص ؛ لأن كمال إيضاح التوحيد الذي هو أشرف المطالب حاصل به ، والحجب الباقية تيسر انكشافه عند انكشافه وآخريته لأن كمال اتضاح التوحيد في مقام أحدية الجمع والفرق ، وهو آخر المقامات فيما يتعارف .

قال الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه : [ اعلم أن أعظم الشبه والحجب أن التعدّدات الواقعة في الوجود الواحد توجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه ، فتوهم  “ 1  “ أن الأعيان ظهرت في الوجود وبالوجود ،

patches.title: Qurʾānic proof, divine freedom, and the opening of Text Twenty-Two

patches.en:
**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—whereas only their effects have appeared in existence. They themselves have not appeared and never will appear, because their very selves do not entail manifestation.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This is the greatest of the doubts that veil divine unity because all the veils of deficiency, possibility, and changes branch from this one. Once it is removed, it is as though all have been removed.

He means that these multiplicities are only the effects of the fixed entities within the one existence that is manifest through them. They therefore give the impression that it is the entities that have appeared in existence and are what is seen, and that they have appeared through an existence peculiar to them, other than the existence of the Necessary. He rejects this: what is manifest in them and through them is the Real. Only the effects of the entities have appeared within that one existence. Those entities have not appeared and never will appear, because in themselves they do not entail—that is, do not admit—manifestation. They are nonexistent things, and nonexistence has no manifestation. Rather, existence is the Manifest and the Hidden.

Hence Shaykh Muḥyī al-Dīn said in *Inshāʾ al-dawāʾir*: “Existence is not something additional to existence,” because existence is what is manifest. This does not contradict its being additional to quiddity in what is other than the Necessary. He then explains how to interpret statements of the realized knowers that differ from this, in the shaykh's words—may God exalt his station:

**Qūnawī:** “Whenever a realized knower reports otherwise, or ascribes existence and manifestation to those entities, that report is in the language of certain ranks and relative tastes. That is, its correctness is established only in relation to a particular station, or particular stations, short of the taste of the station of perfection. As for the definitive text whose ruling is not abrogated, it is what we have stated. The same applies to everything mentioned in this book: it is the explicit truth according to which the matter is. What is said otherwise may be correct without qualification, as is what we have stated here; or it may be correct in relation and attribution to a certain station, as already indicated.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, whenever a realized knower reports from his unveiling something other than our statement that manifestation belongs to existence—for example, saying that manifestation belongs to the entities and that existence is realized in them, or ascribing both existence and manifestation to them and saying that they possess relative existence, which is the shadow of true existence, and that they are what is manifest through it—he reports only in the language of certain ranks of unveiling and certain relative tastes. This does not mean that a reporter who has unveiled all the stations reports in this way from some of them. It means that these words are correct from their speaker only when he has reached a particular station, or particular stations, and is confined to them, without having reached the station of perfection. One who has reached it takes no account of the entities' manifestation or existence: rather, the one existence is what is manifest within them.

وإنما ظهرت آثارها في الوجود ولم تظهر هي ، ولا تظهر أبدا ؛ لأنها ذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور ] . 

إنما كان هذا أعظم الشبه الحاجبة عن التوحيد ؛ لأن جميع الحجب من النقص والإمكان والتغييرات فرع هذا ، فإذا ارتفع ، فكأنه ارتفع الكل . 

يعنى : أن هذه التعددات إنما هي آثار الأعيان الثابتة في الوجود الواحد الظاهر بها ، فتوهم أن الأعيان هي التي ظهرت في الوجود ، فهي المرئية ، وظهرت بوجود خاص لها غير وجود الواجب ، فرد ذلك بأن الظاهر هو الحق فيها وبها ، وإنما ظهرت آثار الأعيان في ذلك الوجود الواحد ، ولم تظهر تلك الأعيان ولا تظهر أبدا ؛ لأنها بالذات لا تقتضي ، 
أي : لا تقبل الظهور ؛ لأنها أمور عدمية ولا ظهور للعدم بل الوجود هو الظاهر والباطن . 
ومن هنا قال الشيخ محيي الدين في  “ إنشاء الدوائر  “  “ 1  “ : إن الوجود ليس بزائد على الوجود ؛ لأن الوجود هو الظاهر ، ولا ينافي كونه زائدا على الماهية في غير الواجب ، ثم ذكر تأويل ما يخالفه من أقوال المحققين ، 

بما قال الشيخ أعلى اللّه مقامه : [ ومتى أخبر محقق بغير هذا أو نسب إليها الوجود والظهور ، فإنما ذلك الإخبار بلسان بعض المراتب والأذواق النسبية ، أي : إنما يثبت صحتها بالنسبة إلى مقام معين ، أو مقامات مخصوصة دون ذوق مقام الكمال ، وأما النص الذي لا ينسخ حكمه ، فهو ما ذكرناه وهكذا كل ما ذكر في هذا الكتاب ، فإنه الحق الصريح الذي هو الأمر عليه ، وما سواه ، فقد يكون صحيحا مطلقا كهذا الذي ذكرنا ، وقد يكون صحيحا بالنسبة والإضافة إلي مقام ما ، كما سبقت الإشارة إليه ] . 
أي : ومتى أخبر محقق عن كشفه بغير ما ذكرنا من أن الظهور للوجود ، بأن قال : 
الظهور لها والوجود محقق فيها ، أو نسب إليها الوجود والظهور جميعا ، وقال لها : الوجود الإضافي هو ظل الوجود الحق ، وهي الظاهرة بذلك الوجود ، فإنما ذلك الإخبار بلسان بعض مراتب الكشف وبلسان بعض الأذواق النسبية لا بمعنى أن المخبر المكاشف بجميع المقامات يخبر بذلك عن بعضها ، بل بمعنى أن هذا الكلام ، إنما يصح من المخبر بها إذا بلغ مقاما معينا ، أو مقامات مخصوصة وتقيد بها ، ولم يصل إلى مقام الكمال ، فإن الواصل إليه لا يعتد بظهورها ولا وجودها ، بل الظاهر هو الوجود الواحد فيها .

patches.title: The effects of the fixed entities and the language of relative stations

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** This is the definitive text that nothing higher abrogates, unlike those stations, which are abrogated by what is higher than they are. He then states that all his definitive texts proceed from the station of perfection and are correct without qualification. This differs from what is mentioned in his other books and in the books of others: that may or may not be so, although it must be correct in relation and attribution to some station. The earlier indication, in the third subdivision of the first three texts, was that all unveilings must be correct in some respect.

If it is asked, “It has been stated repeatedly that the entities are manifest,” we answer: what is meant is their manifestation through the Real's manifestation within them, not through their own selves, just as their existence is in this way. That manifestation and existence are the Real Himself, not the entities; the entities are forever nonexistent.

If it is asked, “Then this would not be one of the definitive texts,” we answer: it would fail to be one of the definitive texts only on the assumption that manifestation [occurs] through their very selves. Otherwise, this statement admits no abrogation. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “When what I have mentioned in this text becomes clear to you, you will know that manifestation is in existence, but on condition of multiplicity together with the effects of the entities within it; and that hiddenness is an intrinsic attribute of the entities, and also of existence insofar as its unity is conceived. The matter turns between manifestation and hiddenness, predominance and subordination: what diminishes from the manifest is included in the hidden, and conversely. Relations and attributions are forms of states and rulings that arise among the ranks. Some make others manifest, and some conceal others, according to the predominance and subordination just indicated. Understand.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** O God, bless our master Muḥammad and his family and companions, and grant them peace. That is, [when] what I have mentioned becomes clear to you—that manifestation belongs to the effects of the entities within existence—you know that manifestation belongs to existence. For the entities have no effect insofar as they are themselves, because they are nonexistent, but only insofar as existence is connected with them. The effects are therefore, in reality, the effects of existence on condition of the entities. “Then, when the effects of existence become manifest on condition of—”

**[The sentence ends at this point in the 2008 printed edition.]**

“Its end; and praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.”

هذا هو النص الذي لا ينسخ بما هو أعلى منه ، بخلاف تلك المقامات فإنها تنسخ بما هي أعلى منها ، ثم ذكر أن جميع نصوصه إنما هي على مقام الكمال وصحتها على الإطلاق ، بخلاف المذكور في غيره من كتبه وكتب غيره ، فإنه قيد يكون كذلك وقد لا يكون ، مع أنه لا بدّ وأن يكون صحيحا ، والإضافة إلى مقام ما سبقت الإشارة في التفريع الثالث من تفاريع النصوص الثلاثة : الأول من أن جميع الكشوف لا بدّ من صحتها بوجه . 
فإن قيل : قد مر مرارا أن الأعيان ظاهرة ، قلنا : المراد ظهورها بظهور الحق فيها ، لا بذاتها ، كما أن وجودها كذلك ، وذلك الظهور والوجود عين الحق لا هي ، فهي معدومة أبدا . 
فإن قيل : فحينئذ لا يكون ذلك من النصوص . 
قلنا : إنما لا يكون من النصوص على تقدير أن يقال : أن الظهور إما بذاتها وإلا فهذا الكلام لا يقبل النسخ ، فافهم . 

قال الشيخ : [ ومتى وضح لك ما ذكرته في هذا النص ، علمت أن الظهور في الوجود ؛ لكن بشرط التعدد مع آثار الأعيان فيه ، وأن البطون صفة ذاتية للأعيان ، والوجود أيضا من حيث تعقل وحدته  “ 1  “ ، والأمر دائر بين الظهور ، وبطون غلبة ومغلوبية ، بمعنى أنه ما نقص من الظاهر ، اندرج في الباطن ، وبالعكس والنسب والإضافات صور أحوال وأحكام تنشأ بين المراتب ، فيظهر بعضها بعضا ، ويخفى بعضها بعضا بحسب الغلبية والمغلوبية المشار إليها آنفا ، فافهم ] . 

وصلّ اللهم على سيدنا محمد وآله وصحبه وسلّم ، أي : وما ظهر لك ما ذكرته من أن الظهور لآثار الأعيان في الوجود ، علمت أن الظهور للوجود ، إذ لا أثر للأعيان من حيث هي ؛ لأنها معدومة ، بل من حيث تعلق الوجود بها فالآثار في الحقيقة آثار الوجود بشرط الأعيان ، فإذا ظهرت آثار الوجود بشرط . 
آخره والحمد لله رب العالمين

patches.editorial_note_append: The physical print witness (printed p. 232 = PDF page 231, zero-based leaf 230) itself stops after فإذا ظهرت آثار الوجود بشرط, followed by the end formula. The interruption is not merely a defect of the online transcription. Its prior cause is unestablished; no manuscript or independent commentary edition was collated. The lemma reads الظهور في الوجود (manifestation is in existence), while the later gloss and the appendix p. 267 read الظهور للوجود (manifestation belongs to existence). These readings are kept distinct. The difficult printed phrases أن الظهور إما بذاتها and وما ظهر لك are rendered syntactically with minimal brackets, without claiming an Arabic emendation. The final formula is recorded without assigning it conclusively to the author or an earlier copyist/editor.
